ITQAN:v3p266/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p266/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p266/r3.claim: The hāʾ in لهب is read with either fatḥa or sukūn in 111:1, but only fatḥa in 111:3 to maintain the rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p266/r3.anchor: ونظير ذلك قراءة ﴿ تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب ﴾ بفتح الهاء وسكونها ولم يقرأ

BURSEVI:v10p411/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r1.claim: Tabbat means she was destroyed; tabāb can also mean loss that leads to destruction.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r1.anchor: فإن التباب الهلاك ومنه قولهم أشابة أم تابة أهالكة من الهرم والعجز أو خسرت فإن التباب أيضا خسران يؤدي إلى الهلاك

BURSEVI:v10p411/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r2.claim: Lahab is a flame or its heat; Abu Lahab was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā’s kunya, explained by his rosy, fiery cheeks or wealth, not a son named Lahab.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r2.anchor: تسكن الهاء كنية عبد العز بن عبد المطلب لجماله أو لماله

BURSEVI:v10p411/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r3.claim: After the command to warn his nearest kin, the Prophet called Quraysh to Ṣafā, asked whether they would believe a warning of an approaching army, and then warned them of the Hour.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r3.anchor: لما روى أنه لما نزل وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين رقى رسول الله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p411/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r4.claim: Abu Lahab answered with a curse and seized a stone to throw at the Prophet, but God prevented him from doing so.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r4.anchor: فقال عمه أبو لهب تبا لك يعني هلاكت باد

BURSEVI:v10p411/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r5.claim: The wording about Abu Lahab’s hands is literal because he tried to throw a stone; describing them as destroyed is apt, while loss rebuts his belief that harming the Prophet profited him.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r5.anchor: فلا كناية في ذكر اليدين ووجه وصف يديه بالهلاك ظاهر وأما

BURSEVI:v10p411/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r10.claim: The kunya is not honorific: it may avoid his ugly idolatrous name or, more pointedly, call him a man of Hell because his name evokes flame.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r10.anchor: أو لكراهة ذكر اسمه القبيح إذ فيه إضافة إلى الصنم أو للتعريض بكونه جهنميا لأنه سيصلى نارا ذات لهب

BURSEVI:v10p411/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p411/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p411/r11.claim: Al-Itqān says Abu Lahab is the Quran’s only person identified by a kunya; the commentary explains that his personal name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā is religiously forbidden.
BURSEVI:v10p411/r11.anchor: قال في الاتقان ليس في القرآن من الكنى غير أبي لهب ولم يذكر اسمه وهو عبد العزى أي الصنم لأنه حرام شرعا

QASHANI:111:1-4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:111:1-4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:111:1-4/r1.claim: Abu Lahab’s hands, the cause of his evil deeds, perish, and his evil self perishes according to its own readiness; he deserves fire by essence and quality, and his kunya signals permanent attachment to it.
QASHANI:111:1-4/r1.anchor: هلك ما هو سبب عمله الخبيث الذي استحق به الجهنمي الملازم لنار الهلاك وهلك ذاته الخبيثة لاستحقاقها بحسب استعدادها

QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r1.claim: For sinners the basmala repairs their deeds and fulfills hopes; for knowers it makes their states seem small, strips them away, and grants union after their annihilation.
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r1.anchor: بسم الله ' كلمة جبارة للمذنبين ، تجبر أعمالهم ، وتحقق آمالهم ، وهي للعارفين تصغر في

QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r2.claim: Abu Lahab's hands were ruined and he himself ruined.

QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r7.claim: Woe to anyone who fails to know Muhammad's worth: wealth cannot help his opponent against the one God has exalted, whose end and his wife's is disgrace.
QUSHAYRI:v3p459/r7.anchor: ويقال : سحقا لمن لا يعرف قدرك - يا محمد . وبعدا لمن لم يشهد ما خصصناك به

SULAMI:v2p426/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p426/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p426/r1.claim: One who failed to recognize the Prophet's nearness, proximity, prophethood, and love suffered manifest loss and went far astray.
SULAMI:v2p426/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر رحمه الله : ظهر حيران من لم ينزلك المنزلة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r1.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r1.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr says that after the chapter was revealed, Abu Lahab's wife arrived shouting with a stone and reciting an insult; the Prophet said she would not see him, and Qur'an shielded him, citing the veil passage.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r1.anchor: عن اسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت : لما نزلت : تبت يدا أبي لهب اقبلت العوراء أم جميل بنت حرب

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r2.claim: After the command to warn his nearest relatives, the Prophet called Quraysh together at Safa and warned them of punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him, and the chapter was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت وانذر عشيرتك الاقربين ورهطك منهم المخلصين ، خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى صعد الصفا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says tabbat means she lost or perished, and tabba means he lost or perished.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في تبت يدا أبي لهب قال خسرت وتب قال خسر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says Abu Lahab was so named because of his handsome appearance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3472#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال انما سمي أبا لهب من حسنه

TUSTARI:111:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:111:1/r1.claim: The first loss concerns Abu Lahab's wealth and the second his soul; the rest of the surah explains the loss.
TUSTARI:111:1/r1.anchor: أي خسر، فالخسران الأول خسران المال، والخسران الآخر خسران النفس،

TUSTARI:111:2/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:111:2/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:111:2/r2.claim: An alternate reading takes the first statement as a curse and the second as a report of loss fixed by prior decree, answering Abu Lahab's curse when Muhammad summoned his clan to monotheism and warned them.
TUSTARI:111:2/r2.anchor: وفيها وجه آخر: أن يكون التباب الأول كالدعاء عليه، والثاني كالإخبار عن وقوع الخسران في سابق التقدير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r1.claim: The sura is called Tabbat in most codices and by al-Tirmidhi and many exegetes, after its opening word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r1.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في أكثر المصاحف ( سورة تبت ) وكذلك عنونها الترمذي في ( جامعه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r2.claim: Some codices and tafsirs call it al-Masad; many exegetes call it Sura of Abu Lahab, while Abu Hayyan uses al-Lahab.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r2.anchor: وسميت في بعض المصاحف وبعض التفاسير ( سورة المسد ) . واقتصر في ( الإتقان ) على هذين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi's title What Happened to Abu Lahab is only a descriptive heading, not the sura's name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r3.anchor: وسماها جمع من المفسرين ( سورة أبي لهب ) على تقدير : سورة ذكر أبي لهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r4.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus, fifth in verse count, and sixth in revelation order after al-Fatiha and before al-Takwir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r4.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . وعدت السادسة من السور نزولا ، نزلت بعد سورة الفاتحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r5.claim: A report dates its revelation to the fourth year of the mission; the two Sahih collections relate the occasion at Safa, where Abu Lahab cursed the Prophet after his warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r5.anchor: روي أن نزولها كان في السنة الرابعة من البعثة . وسبب نزولها على ما في ( الصحيحين ) عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r6.claim: His report from Ibn Abbas gives the same Safa incident and ties it to the command to warn the nearest kin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r6.anchor: ووقع في ( الصحيحين ) من رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r7.claim: Because the cited nearest-kin verse in al-Shuara was revealed later, the report is resolved by Abu Usama's version, which omits its sura attribution: an earlier similar verse had been revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p599/r7.anchor: وتأويل ذلك أن آية تشبه آية سورة الشعراء نزلت قبل سورة أبي لهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r1.claim: Opening with ruin is a rhetorical prelude to a sura of rebuke and threat, like the opening warning of woe for defrauders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r1.anchor: افتتاح السورة بالتبات مشعر بأنها نزلت لتوبيخ ووعيد ، فذلك براعة استهلال مثل ما تفتتح أشعار الهجاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن الحكم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r2.claim: His cited invective begins by calling down ruin, illustrating the hostile opening convention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r2.anchor: قول عبد الرحمن بن الحكم من شعراء ( الحماسة ) : لحا الله قيسا قيس عيلان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r3.speaker: أبو تمام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r3.claim: His invective likewise opens with a string of threats and disasters as a hostile prelude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r3.anchor: وقول أبي تمام في طالعة هجاء : النار والعار والمكروه والعطب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن الخازن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r4.claim: He adapts Abu Tammam's opening in a congratulatory poem for a birth, showing the opening technique can suit praise too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r4.anchor: ومنه أخذ أبو بكر بن الخازن قوله في طالع قصيدة هناء بمولد : مجشري فقد أنجز الإقبال ما وعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r5.claim: Tabb means ruin and destruction; the wording is both a curse and rebuke, answering Abu Lahab's insult with fitting requital.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r5.anchor: والتب : الخسران والهلاك ، والكلام دعاء وتقريع لأبي لهب دافع الله به عن نبيئه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r6.claim: The hands are singled out because Abu Lahab reportedly insulted the Prophet and seized a stone to throw at him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r6.anchor: وإسناد التب إلى اليدين لما روي من أن أبا لهب لما قال للنبيء : ( تبا لك سائر اليوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r7.speaker: طارق المحاربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r7.claim: He recounts seeing Muhammad preach at Dhu al-Majaz while Abu Lahab followed, injured his legs, and called him a liar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن طارق المحاربي قال : ( بينا أنا بسوق ذي المجاز إذا أنا برجل حديث السن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r8.claim: The curse falls on the hands because they caused the Prophet's injury, as Arabic idioms also curse or praise a person's mouth and hands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r8.anchor: فوقع الدعاء على يديه لأنهما سبب أذى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما يقال للذي يتكلم بمكروه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r9.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r9.claim: His verse calls down God's punishment on hands, illustrating the curse's conventional reference to the instrument of harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r9.anchor: وقول النابغة : قعود الذي أبياتهم يثمدونهم رمى الله في تلك الأكف الكوانع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r10.claim: The positive converse appears in a blessing that the speaker's mouth not be chipped and an Asadi man's prayer for Musawwar's hands after he aided him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p600#2/r10.anchor: ويقال بضد ذلك للذي يقول كلاما حسنا : لا فض فوك ، وقال أعرابي من بني أسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح بن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r1.claim: He allows a proper name to change its usual vowel after becoming a proper name, as in compounds such as Maadd Yakrib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r1.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جني في كتاب ( إعراب الحماسة ) : ( يجوز أن يكون ضم الشين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r2.claim: Abu Salma, with a damma, likewise transfers the feminine name Salma to the name of Zuhayr's father, since men are rarely given women's kunyas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r2.anchor: وكما قالوا : أبو سلمى بضم السين كنية والد زهير بن أبي سلمى لأنهم نقلوا اسم سلمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r4.claim: وَتَبَ may coordinate a second curse with تبت يدا; if the hands are the instrument of harm, the second curse covers Abu Lahab wholly and intensifies the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r4.anchor: وجملة : { وتب } إما معطوفة على جملة : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } عطف الدعاء على الدعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r5.claim: The whole-person curse is coordinated with the part because they differ in scope; verbal emphasis of identical wording would not take a coordinating waw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r5.anchor: وتفيد بذلك تأكيدا لجملة : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } لأنها بمعناها ، وإنما اختلفتا بالكلية والجزئية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r6.claim: Alternatively, wa-tab is a circumstantial assertion rather than a curse, meaning the called-down ruin has in fact occurred, as in al-Nabigha's verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r6.anchor: وإما أن تكون في موضع الحال ، والواو واو الحال ولا تكون دعاء إنما هي تحقيق لحصول ما دعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r7.claim: His reading adds وقد تب, supporting the interpretation that the preceding statement expresses contempt rather than a prayer for ruin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r7.anchor: ويؤيد هذا الوجه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود ( وقد تب ) فيتمحض الكلام قبله لمعنى الذم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r8.claim: His poem about his own death uses a similar circumstantial construction to convey a confirmed outcome, not a curse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p602/r8.anchor: كقول عبد الله بن رواحة حين خروجه إلى غزوة مؤتة التي استشهد فيها : حتى يقولوا إذا مروا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r1.claim: After the command to warn his nearest relatives (26:214), the Prophet called Safiyya and Fatima, saying he could not save them from God and inviting them to ask for his wealth; then he summoned Quraysh at Safa, warned them of punishment, and Abu Lahab cursed him, after which the surah came down.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r1.anchor: روي في الحديث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت عليه:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r2.claim: Tabbat means she lost; tabab means loss and destruction. The hands stand for earning, gaining, and holding possessions, and the second phrase makes his ruin certain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r2.anchor: وتبت معناه: خسرت، والتباب: الخسار والدمار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud’s reading adds qad, ‘already,’ to the statement that Abu Lahab perished.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r3.anchor: ففي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: «تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r4.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet’s paternal uncle, ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, but had been destined for misery.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r4.anchor: و «أبو لهب» : هو عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب، وهو عم النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin read Abu Lahab with a silent h; the other readers vocalize it, and all retain fatḥa in ‘a blazing fire.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p534#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن: «أبي لهب» بسكون الهاء،

AKHFASH:v2p588/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p588/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p588/r1.claim: Tabbat has the feminine tāʾ form that al-Akhfash calls jazm, as in ḍaraba/ḍarabat; tabba is an open-vowel masculine past verb.
AKHFASH:v2p588/r1.anchor: جزم لأن تاء المؤنث اذا كانت في الفعل فهو جزم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p256#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p256#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p256#2/r6.claim: In a report graded by al-Bukhari and Muslim as being in their Ṣaḥīḥayn, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet summoned Quraysh at al-Safa after 26:214, warned them of punishment, and Abu Lahab cursed him and objected; this occasioned the surah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p256#2/r6.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين من حديث سعيد ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال لما نزل وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r1.claim: Tabbat means Abu Lahab's hands were ruined, while wa-tabb says that he himself was ruined.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r1.anchor: ومعنى تبت خسرت يدا أبي لهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads the first clause as a curse and the second as a report that it came true, like a curse followed by its fulfillment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r2.anchor: قال الفراء الأول دعاء والثاني خبر كما يقول الرجل أهلكك الله وقد أهلكك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r3.claim: Mentioning Abu Lahab's two hands stands for his whole self, an Arab usage of naming a part for the whole.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r3.anchor: ذكر يديه والمراد نفسه ولكن هذا عادة العرب يعبرون ببعض الشيء عن جميعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r4.claim: He illustrates the part-for-whole expression with the verse about what one's hands have sent ahead.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the ruined hands and ruin as referring to Abu Lahab's children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب ولد أبي لهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r6.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's paternal uncle; it is said his personal name was Abd al-Uzza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r6.anchor: فأما أبو لهب فهو عم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل إن اسمه عبد العزى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir alone reads the hāʾ of Abī Lahab with sukūn; Abu Ali likens this to dialect variants in other words.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحده أبي لهب بإسكان الهاء قال أبو علي يشبه أن يكون لغة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r8.claim: Asked why God used Abu Lahab's honorific, the first answer is that if his name was Abd al-Uzza, naming him that way would invoke a name carrying shirk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r8.anchor: أحدهما أنه إن صح أن اسمه عبد العزى فكيف يذكره الله بهذا الأسم وفيه معنى الشرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r9.claim: A second answer is that many people are known by their kunyas and their personal names are unknown.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r9.anchor: والثاني أن كثيرا من الناس اشتهروا بكناهم ولم يعرف لهم أسماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba transmits from al-Asmaʿi that Abu Amr and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Ala disliked their kunyas; if Abu Lahab's personal name was his kunya, it was the name by which he was known.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p259/r10.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة خبرني غير واحد عن الأصمعي أن أبا عمرو بن العلاء وأبا سفيان ابن العلاء أساؤهما كناهما

FARRA:v3p298/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p298/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p298/r1.claim: The Prophet called his clan together at al-Marwa to warn them; Abū Lahab challenged him and cursed him, and the chapter was revealed.
FARRA:v3p298/r1.anchor: الله عليه وسلم قام على المروة، فقال: يا آل غالب، فاجتمعت إليه،

FARRA:v3p298/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p298/r2.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p298/r2.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh’s reading, qad tabb in the first clause is a prayer, while the final tabb is a report.
FARRA:v3p298/r2.anchor: لهب وتب» وفى قراءة عبد الله: «وقد تب» فالأول: دعاء، والثاني: خبر.

FARRA:v3p298/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p298/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p298/r3.claim: Tabba means “he lost”: it can be a curse followed by a statement that the loss occurred.
FARRA:v3p298/r3.anchor: خبر. قال الفراء: «تب» : خسر، كما تقول للرجل: أهلكك الله، وقد أهلكك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r1.claim: The Prophet warned Quraysh from Mount Safa that a severe punishment was coming; Abu Lahab cursed him, and the chapter was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله: {تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r2.claim: The first clause is a prayer against Abu Lahab, while the second states as fact that he was ruined.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r2.anchor: الأول دعاء عليه، والثاني خبر عنه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r3.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's uncle, Abd al-Uzza b. Abd al-Muttalib, kunya Abu Utba; he was called Abu Lahab for his bright face and persistently abused the Prophet and his religion.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r4.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r4.claim: Rabi'a recalls seeing the Prophet call people to profess God's oneness at the market of Dhu al-Majaz while his uncle followed, calling him a lying Sabian.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r5.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي عن أبيه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r5.claim: A parallel account says Abu Lahab followed the Prophet among tribes and warned them that he wanted them to abandon al-Lat and al-Uzza for a false innovation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p514#2/r5.anchor: هذا يريد منكم أن تسلخوا اللات والعزى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515/r1.claim: “May Abu Lahab's hands perish” means he failed and lost, his effort wasted; “and he perished” confirms his ruin.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r11.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r11.claim: A report says Umm Jamil came raging with a stone to Abu Bakr while the Prophet sat unseen beside him, reciting a taunt; he was protected by a veil linked to 17:45.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r11.anchor: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r12.speaker: أم حكيم بنت عبد المطلب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r12.claim: When Umm Jamil stumbled while circling the House and cursed “Mudhammam,” Umm Hakim answered with a boast about her chastity, strength, and kinship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p515#2/r12.anchor: إني لحصان فما أكلم، وثقاف فما أعلم،

JISHUMI:v10p7583/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir gives the h in Abu Lahab a sukun; other readers give it a fatha, and everyone agrees on the fatha in ذات لهب.
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير. أبي لهب ساكنة الهاء، الباقون بفتحها

JISHUMI:v10p7583/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r7.claim: The common reading has wa-tabb as a curse, while Ibn Masud reads wa-qad tabb as a statement that the ruin has happened, like a prayer followed by its fulfillment.
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r7.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: (وقد تب)، فالأول دعاء، والثاني خبر

JISHUMI:v10p7583/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r10.claim: The feminine tā' in tabbat is quiescent in a non-address form and reflects the feminine dual hands; tab is masculine because it is attached to Abu Lahab.
JISHUMI:v10p7583/r10.anchor: وأنث (تبت): لإضافته إلى اليدين، وهي مؤنثة، (وتب) ذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r1.claim: Tabb means destruction; the proverb about an old woman being tāb describes someone ruined by age and infirmity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r1.anchor: التباب : الهلاك . ومنه قولهم : أشابة أم تابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r2.claim: His two hands were ruined because he took a stone to throw at the Prophet; “and he perished” extends this to his whole person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r2.anchor: أخذ حجرا ليرمي به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { وتب } وهلك كله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r3.claim: Alternatively, “hands” stands for the whole person, as in the Qurʾanic idiom “because of what your hands have sent ahead.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r3.anchor: أو جعلت يداه هالكتين . والمراد : هلاك جملته ، كقوله تعالى : { بما قدمت يداك }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819/r4.claim: The second verb can mean the destruction actually happened, supported by Ibn Masud’s reading وقد تب and a poetic parallel.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r1.claim: When ordered to warn his nearest kin, the Prophet called the clans at Safa; Abu Lahab cursed him for summoning them and the sūra was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r1.anchor: أنه لما نزل { وأنذر عشيرتك الاقربين } ( الشعراء : 214 ) رقى الصفا وقال : يا صباحاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r2.claim: Abu Lahab is named by his best-known appellation to make the curse unmistakable and lasting; people may be identified by either name or kunya.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r2.anchor: قلت : فيه ثلاثة أوجه ، أحدها : أن يكون مشتهرا بالكنية دون الاسم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r3.claim: A supporting reading uses أبو in nominative form; examples show that famous names and kunyas can be preserved without grammatical alteration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r3.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك قراءة : من قرأ يدا أبو لهب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r4.claim: Another reason is that his original name was Abd al-Uzza, so the Qurʾan used his kunya instead.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى ، فعدل عنه إلى كنيته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r5.claim: His kunya also suits his destiny in a blazing fire; it may mock his glowing cheeks and pride in them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r5.anchor: والثالث : أنه لما كان من أهل النار ومآله إلى نار ذات لهب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r6.claim: Other kunyas name people for traits, and the Prophet called Abu al-Muhallab Abu Safra for the yellowness of his face.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r6.anchor: ويقال : أبو لهب ، كما يقال : أبو الشر للشرير . وأبو الخير للخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r7.claim: Read أبي لهب with a silent bāʾ, as in altered proper-name pronunciations such as Shams ibn Malik.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( أبي لهب ) بالسكون . وهو من تغيير الأعلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r8.claim: ما أغنى is an incredulous question or a negation; وما كسب may mean his earnings or what he acquired.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r8.anchor: ما أغنى } استفهام في معنى الإنكار ، ومحله النصب أو نفي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r9.claim: “His wealth and what he earned” may mean capital and profits, livestock and its offspring, inherited and self-earned property, or old and new wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r9.anchor: والمعنى : لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله ، يعني : رأس المال والأرباح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets what Abu Lahab earned as his children.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ما كسب ولده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r11.claim: Abu Lahab once called his sons evil earnings after one pushed him while he tried to break up their fight; a Prophetic report says a son is a man’s earning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r11.anchor: وحكى أن بني أبي لهب احتكموا إليه ، فاقتتلوا ، فقام يحجز بينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r12.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says the wealth and earnings include his evil efforts to oppose the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r12.anchor: وعن الضحاك : ما ينفعه ماله وعمله الخبيث ، يعني كيده في عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r13.claim: Qatada says his “earnings” are the deeds he imagined would benefit him, as in the verse about deeds made like scattered dust.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r13.anchor: وعن قتادة : عمله الذي ظن أنه منه على شيء ، كقوله : { وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r14.claim: Abu Lahab reportedly claimed that if his nephew were truthful, he could ransom himself from punishment with his wealth and children.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r14.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r15.claim: سيصلى is read with a fatḥa or ḍamma on yāʾ, in light or doubled form; the future particle threatens an inevitable punishment, even if delayed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r15.anchor: ( سيصلى ) قرىء : بفتح الياء وبضمها مخففا ومشددا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r16.claim: Abu Lahab’s wife was Umm Jamil, daughter of Harb and sister of Abu Sufyan; she scattered thorny plants on the Prophet’s path at night.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r16.anchor: هي أم جميل بنت حرب أخت أبي سفيان ، وكانت تحمل حزمة من الشوك والحسك والسعدان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r17.claim: Alternatively, carrying firewood means carrying malicious gossip that kindles discord between people; the cited verse’s “moist firewood” evokes smoke and intensified strife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p819#2/r17.anchor: وقيل : كانت تمشى بالنميمة ويقال : للمشاء بالنمائم المفسد بين الناس : يحمل الحطب بينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r1.claim: The wife is coordinated with the subject of سيصلى, so both he and she will burn; alternatively, the phrase about her neck is a new subject and predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r1.anchor: ورفعت عطفا على الضمير في { سيصلى } أي : سيصلى هو وامرأته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r2.claim: The accusative reading حمالة الحطب is an insult, and al-Zamakhshari explicitly prefers it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( حمالة الحطب ) بالنصب على الشتم ؛ وأنا أستحب هذه القراءة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r3.claim: Other readings vary the form to حمالة الحطب or حمالة للحطب, with tanwin and nominative or accusative, and a diminutive form مريته.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r3.anchor: وقرىء : ( حمالة الحطب ) وحمالة للحطب : بالتنوين ، والرفع والنصب . وقرىء : ( ومريته ) بالتصغير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r4.claim: Masad is tightly twisted cord made from palm fiber, leather, or other materials; a poetic phrase describes a tightly formed body.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r4.anchor: المسد : الذي فتل من الحبال فتلا شديدا ، من ليف كان أو جلد ، أو غيرهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r5.claim: The image has her tie a thorn bundle around her neck like a woodcutter, degrading her despite her noble and wealthy household and provoking her husband.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r5.anchor: والمعنى : في جيدها حبل مما مسد من الحبال ، وأنها تحمل تلك الحزمة من الشوك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r6.claim: Alternatively, her punishment mirrors her deed: she will bear firewood from the Tree of Zaqqum or Dariʿ with a chain of fire around her neck.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى : أن حالها تكون من نار جهنم على الصورة التي كانت عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r7.claim: The Prophet expressed hope that whoever recites the sūra will not be gathered with Abu Lahab in the same abode.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p821/r7.anchor:
وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :
( 1370 ) ( من قرأ سورة تبت رجوت أن لا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب

MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p315#2/r1.anchor: «تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب» (1) أبو لهب..

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r1.claim: Abu Lahab asked what he would receive if he accepted Islam; when told the same as other Muslims, he rejected a faith that made them equal, and the surah was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن أبا لهب أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ماذا أعطى إن آمنت بك يا محمد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r2.claim: After 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet summoned the people from Safa and warned that an army was approaching; Abu Lahab cursed him, prompting this surah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : ما رواه ابن عباس أنه لما نزل { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r3.claim: Al-Kaysan reports that Abu Lahab would turn visiting delegations away by calling Muhammad a liar, sorcerer, or mad; one group insisted on meeting him, and the Prophet became distressed when he heard Abu Lahab’s abuse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان أنه كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفد انطلق إليهم أبو لهب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tabbat as having failed or been frustrated.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r5.claim: Ata glosses tabbat as having strayed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr glosses tabbat as having perished.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r7.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r7.claim: Yaman ibn Ri’ab glosses tabbat as being emptied of all good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p363#2/r7.anchor: الرابع : صفرت من كل خير , قاله يمان بن رئاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r1.claim: Qatada gives “lost” as a fifth gloss of tabbat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r2.claim: A cited poem uses tabban in a line about a people who failed to fulfill their vow.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r2.anchor: ولم يوفوا بنذرهم فيا تبا لما صعنوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r3.claim: “Abu Lahab’s hands” can mean Abu Lahab himself, using hand for the person; 22:10 similarly says what one’s hands have sent ahead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r3.anchor: يعني نفس أبي لهب , وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد كما قال تعالى { ذلك بما قدمت يداك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r4.claim: Alternatively, the hands mean Abu Lahab’s deeds, since most actions are done by hand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r4.anchor: الثاني : أي عمل أبي لهب , وإنما نسب العمل إلى اليد لأنه في الأكثر يكون بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r5.claim: The epithet Abu Lahab may refer to his handsome appearance and glowing cheeks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r5.anchor: وقيل إنه كني أبا لهب لحسنه وتلهب وجنته

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r6.claim: He is named by his kunyah because he was better known by it than by his personal name.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r6.anchor: أحدها : أنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r7.claim: Another explanation is that his personal name was Abd Hashim, or Abd al-Uzza, so the text avoids it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r7.anchor: الثاني : لأنه كان مسمى بعبد هشم , وقيل إنه عبد العزى فلذلك عدل عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r8.claim: A third explanation is that a personal name is more honorable than a kunyah, which refers to someone through another person; God therefore names prophets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r8.anchor: الثالث : لأن الاسم أشرف من الكنية , لأن الكنية إشارة إليه باسم غيره , ولذلك دعا الله أنبياءه بأسمائهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r9.claim: One reading takes the second tabba as emphatic repetition of the first.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r9.anchor: أحدها : أنه تأكيد للأول من قوله { تبت يدا أبي لهب } فقال بعده ( وتب ) تأكيدا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r10.claim: Another explanation says his hands failed to harm the Messenger, while he himself perished through God’s painful punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r10.anchor: الثاني : يعني تبت يدا أبي لهب بما منعه الله تعالى من أذى لرسوله , وتب بما له عند الله من أليم عقابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the second tabba to mean that he has perished.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r11.anchor: الثالث : يعني قد تب , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r12.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r12.claim: Mujahid takes the second tabba as a prediction that Abu Lahab’s son would perish.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r12.anchor: الرابع : يعني وتب ولد أبي لهب , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r13.claim: Ibn Masud’s reading says his hands failed and he has indeed perished, as a declarative report; the other reading is a curse or prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r13.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب , جعله خبرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Lahab’s hands failed in relation to monotheism.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r14.anchor: أحدهما : عن التوحيد , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p364/r15.claim: Mujahid says Abu Lahab’s hands failed in relation to good works.

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r1.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's uncle, named Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r1.anchor: واسمه عبدالعزى بن عبدالمطلب، وهو عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r2.claim: He was called Abu Lahab because his cheeks were red as if fire burned from them.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r2.anchor: وإنما سمي أبو لهب لأن وجنتيه كانتا حمراوين، كأنما يلتهب منهما النار

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r3.claim: After 26:214 commanded warning near relatives, the Prophet asked Ali to prepare food and invite Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r3.anchor: يعني بني هاشم، وبني المطلب، وهما ابنا عبد مناف بن قصى

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r4.claim: Ali prepared one sheep and a bowl of milk for thirty-nine men; they all ate and drank their fill.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r4.anchor: وهم أربعون رجلا غير رجل، على رجل شاة، وعس من لبن، فأكلوا حتى شبعوا

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r5.speaker: أبو لهب
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r5.claim: Abu Lahab accused Muhammad of sorcery, saying ten of their men normally eat a whole sheep and drink a bowl of milk, yet Muhammad fed forty with a sheep and milk.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r5.anchor: لهذا ما سحركم به، الرجال العشرة منا يأكلون الجذعة، ويشربون العس

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r6.claim: The Prophet was distressed and did not warn them that night, so he asked Ali to prepare a second meal; after they ate, he announced he was God's warner and bearer of good news and urged them to believe and obey.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r6.anchor: فلما سمع ذلك منه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شق عليه، ولم ينذرهم تلك الليلة

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r7.speaker: أبو لهب
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r7.claim: Abu Lahab cursed Muhammad for summoning them and then the surah was revealed about him.
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r7.anchor: فقال أبو لهب: تبا لك، يا محمد، سائر اليوم لهذا دعوتنا؟ فأنزل الله عز وجل فيه

MUQATIL:111:1-4/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:111:1-4/r8.claim: “Perished Abu Lahab's hands, and he perished” means that Abu Lahab lost.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r1.claim: Tabbat means destruction; the hands perished because, according to a report, Abū Lahab took a stone to throw at the Prophet, or the wording means his whole person perished as in the idiom about what one's hands earned.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r1.anchor: التباب الهلاك ومنه قولهم أشابه أم تابة أى هالكة من الهرم والمعنى هلكت يداه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r2.claim: The second tabba means he was destroyed and that this had happened; Ibn Masʿūd's reading wa-qad tab supports the completed event.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r2.anchor: ومعنى وتب وكان ذلك وحصل كقوله جزاني جزاه الله شر جزائه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r3.claim: After the command to warn near relatives, the Prophet called people at Ṣafā and warned Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Banū Fihr that he was a warner before the Hour; Abū Lahab cursed him, prompting revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r3.anchor: روى أنه لما نزل وانذر عشيرتك الا قربين رقى الصفا وقال يا صباحاه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r4.claim: Abū Lahab's kunya may be an honorific by which he was widely known, dislike of his name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, or a fitting reference to his future fiery fate.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p361#6/r4.anchor: وإنما كناه والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بها دون الامم أو لكراهة اسمه فاسمه

NAHHAS:v5p305/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p305/r1.claim: Tabbat may be a curse or a statement; the tāʾ may be still because it is a particle or because its vowel was lost.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r1.anchor: في تب الأولى قولان أحدهما أنه دعاء والآخر أنه خبر وفي إسكان التاء قولان

NAHHAS:v5p305/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p305/r2.claim: Yadā may be figurative or literal, recalling the report that Abū Lahab tried to throw something at the Prophet but God stopped him.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r2.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما أنه مجاز أي تب والآخر أنه على الحقيقة كما يروى أن أبا لهب أراد أن يرمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NAHHAS:v5p305/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p305/r3.claim: Kufans say the yāʾ marks the genitive; another account treats the form as a doubly declinable proper name.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r3.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما أن علامة الخفض الياء والقول الآخر أنه معرب من جهتين هذا قول الكوفيين

NAHHAS:v5p305/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v5p305/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to read tabbat yadā Abī Lahab wa-qad tabba.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r4.anchor: كما روي عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ ( تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب )

NAHHAS:v5p305/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p305/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p305/r5.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted qad before tabba; another treats tabba as a direct statement, since qad is not needed with a particle of meaning.
NAHHAS:v5p305/r5.anchor: وتب فيه قولان أحدهما أن فيه قد مضمرة كما روي عن ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r1.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Ibn Abbas says the sura followed the Prophet's call from Mount Safa after 26:214: Quraysh affirmed he never lied, then Abu Lahab cursed him for warning them.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r1.anchor: في الصحيحين وغيرهما واللفظ لمسلم عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r2.speaker: الحميدي وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r2.claim: An added report says Abu Lahab's wife came to the mosque carrying a stone, but God concealed the Prophet from her sight; she threatened him in verse, then left seeing only Abu Bakr.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r2.anchor: زاد الحميدي وغيره: فلما سمعت امرأته ما نزل في زوجها وفيها من القرآن،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r3.claim: Quraysh called the Prophet 'Mudhammam' to abuse him; he said God diverted their harm because they reviled Mudhammam while he was Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r3.anchor: وكانت قريش إنما تسمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مذمما، يسبونه، وكان يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd gives another occasion: Abu Lahab asked what advantage he would receive by becoming Muslim, rejected equality with other Muslims, and the sura was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن سبب نزولها ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r1.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan says Abu Lahab repeatedly turned visiting delegations away by calling the Prophet a liar and sorcerer; when one delegation insisted, he cursed the Prophet, who grieved and received the sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r1.anchor: وقول ثالث حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان قال: كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r2.claim: Another account says Abu Lahab tried to stone the Prophet, God prevented him, and the verse announced that prevention.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن أبا لهب أراد أن يرمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر، فمنعه الله من ذلك،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء، ابن جبير، يمان بن رئاب
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r4.claim: Other explanations gloss the verb as failed, strayed, perished, or became empty of every good.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: خابت قال ابن عباس. وقيل: ضلت قاله عطاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r5.claim: The hands are singled out because most work is done with them: they lost, and Abu Lahab himself lost.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r5.anchor: وخص اليدين بالتباب، لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما أي خسرتا وخسر هو.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, 'hands' stands for the whole person, as in 22:10, and Arabic uses a part for the whole; a poem illustrates the idiom.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: المراد باليدين نفسه. وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r7.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r7.claim: Al-Asma'i reports that a caller after Uthman's killing recited a lament using tabban for the calamity of what people had done.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#2/r7.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان رحمه الله سمع الناس هاتفا يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the first tabbat is a curse and the second a factual report, as in 'May God destroy him; he has perished'; Ubay's and Abdullah's reading adds 'qad'.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: التب الأول: دعاء والثاني خبر، كما يقال: أهلكه الله وقد هلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r2.claim: Abu Lahab's personal name was Abd al-Uzza, and he was the Prophet's paternal uncle; his wife Umm Jamil was Abu Sufyan's sister, and both strongly opposed the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r2.anchor: وأبو لهب اسمه عبد العزى، وهو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r3.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r3.claim: Tariq ibn Abdullah recounts seeing the Prophet preach the testimony of faith at Dhu al-Majaz while Abu Lahab followed him, bloodied his legs with stones, and called him a liar.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r3.anchor: قال طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي: إني بسوق ذي المجاز، إذ أنا بإنسان يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r4.claim: Ata transmits Ibn Abbas's account that Abu Lahab accused Muhammad of magic, while marveling that Muhammad's food and drink satisfied people.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r4.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو لهب: سحركم محمد!

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects using this verse to prove that an unbeliever may receive a respectful kunya; he gives four reasons for God's use of Abu Lahab.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r5.anchor: وقد ظن قوم أن في هذا دليلا على تكنية المشرك وهو باطل،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r6.claim: The four reasons are that his given name invoked an idol, his kunya was better known, a kunya is lower than a proper name, and the name foreshadows his abode in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r6.anchor: الأول: أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى، والعزى: صنم،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r7.claim: Another account says his family called him Abu Lahab for his glowing, handsome face; God turned them from more favorable names such as Abu al-Nur toward the ill-omened fire-name.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r7.anchor: وقد قيل: اسمه كنيته. فكان أهله يسمونه أبا لهب،

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، ابن كثير، ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r8.claim: These readers pronounce the hāʾ in 'Abi Lahab' with sukūn, while preserving it open in 'dhāt lahab' to fit the verse endings.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وابن كثير وابن محيصن. «أبي لهب» بإسكان الهاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when God created the Pen He ordered it to record what would occur, including the doom of Abu Lahab.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما خلق الله عز وجل القلم قال له: اكتب ما هو كائن

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r10.claim: Hasan says Abu Lahab could not escape the Fire, since his fate was written in the Preserved Book before he and his parents were created.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r10.anchor: وقال منصور: سئل الحسن عن قوله تعالى: { تبت يدآ أبي لهب }

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r11.claim: The Adam-and-Moses exchange is cited as a precedent for God's prior decree; the Prophet says Adam prevailed over Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#3/r11.anchor: ويؤيده قول موسى لآدم:أنت الذي خلقك الله بيده، ونفخ فيك من روحه

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r1.claim: In the report from Abu Hurayra through Hammam, Adam asks how long before his creation God wrote the Torah; Moses answers two thousand years, including the statement that Adam disobeyed, so Adam asks why he is blamed for what was decreed.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r1.anchor: وفي حديث همام عن أبي هريرة أن آدم قال لموسى:

QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r2.speaker: طاوس، ابن هرمز، الأعرج عن أبي هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r2.claim: A separate transmission gives forty years, rather than two thousand, for the interval before Adam's creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:111:1#4/r2.anchor: وفي حديث طاووس وابن هرمز والأعرج عن أبي هريرة:

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah has five verses.

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r2.claim: Abu Lahab was Muhammad’s uncle, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; his bright face gave him the nickname Abu Lahab.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r2.anchor: هو عم النبي [ ص ] وإنما سمي أبو لهب لإشراق وجهه

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r3.claim: Umm Jamil, Arwa daughter of Harb ibn Umayya and Abu Sufyan’s sister, supported her husband’s sustained campaign against Muhammad and the message.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r3.anchor: وكانت زوجته أم جميل في عونه في هذه الحملة الدائبة الظالمة .

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r4.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r4.claim: Rabiʿa recalls accompanying his father as a youth, seeing Muhammad preach to tribes while Abu Lahab followed, warning them against abandoning al-Lat and al-ʿUzza for his alleged innovation.

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports Muhammad warned Quraysh from al-Baṭḥāʾ; Abu Lahab retorted, “Was that why you gathered us?”, after which the surah was revealed.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،  أن النبي [ ص ] خرج إلى البطحاء

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r6.claim: A variant says Abu Lahab shook his hands and cursed Muhammad for the rest of the day, again prompting revelation of the surah.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r6.anchor: وفي رواية فقام ينفض يديه وهو يقول : تبا لك سائر اليوم

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r7.claim: When Banu Hashim agreed under Abu Talib to protect Muhammad out of clan solidarity, Abu Lahab defected to Quraysh and joined their boycott document.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r7.anchor: ولما أجمع بنو هاشم بقيادة أبي طالب على حماية النبي [ ص ]

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r8.claim: Abu Lahab had betrothed his sons to Muhammad’s daughters before the mission, then ordered them to divorce the women to burden Muhammad.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r8.anchor: وكان قد خطب بنتي رسول الله [ ص ] رقية وأم كلثوم

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r9.claim: It is reported that Umm Jamil carried thorns and put them in Muhammad’s path.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r9.anchor: وقد روي أن أم جميل كانت تحمل الشوك فتضعه في طريق النبي

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r10.claim: Another explanation takes carrying firewood figuratively as her pursuit of harm, discord, and backbiting against the Prophet.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r10.anchor: وقيل : إن حمل الحطب كناية عن سعيها بالأذى والفتنة والوقيعة

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r11.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r11.claim: The surah answers the public war Abu Lahab and his wife waged; God undertakes the battle on behalf of His Messenger.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r11.anchor: نزلت هذه السورة ترد على هذه الحرب المعلنة من أبي لهب وامرأته .

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r12.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r12.claim: Tabb means ruin, destruction, and severance; the first occurrence is a supplication, the second confirms that it has come to pass.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r12.anchor: والتباب الهلاك والبوار والقطع . ( وتبت )الأولى دعاء . ( وتب )الثانية تقرير

QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r13.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r13.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r13.claim: In a single short opening verse the curse is issued and fulfilled, ending the conflict and drawing its curtain.
QUTB-ZILAL:111:1/r13.anchor: ففي آية قصيرة واحدة في مطلع السورة تصدر الدعوة وتتحقق ،  وتنتهي المعركة ويسدل الستار

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.claim: The creation purpose is worship; al-Kafirun contrasts the Prophet’s obedience and rejection of partners with the unbelievers’ worship of idols, while al-Nasr promises worldly victory and afterlife reward and al-Masad threatens worldly loss and afterlife punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r1.anchor: ثم بين في سورة : { قل ياأهل * أيها * الكافرون }

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r3.claim: When commanded to warn his nearest kin, the Prophet called the Quraysh clans at al-Safa and said he could offer no worldly or afterlife share unless they affirmed God’s unity; Abu Lahab objected, and the surah was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله يكتم أمره في أول المبعث ويصلي في شعاب مكة ثلاث سنين

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r4.claim: In another occasion report, the Prophet called the Quraysh to verify his warning before announcing a severe punishment; Abu Lahab protested and the surah came down.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r4.anchor: صعد الصفا ذات يوم وقال : يا صباحاه

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r5.claim: A third report says the Prophet fed his uncles from a small dish that miraculously fed them all, then invited them to Islam; Abu Lahab objected that Muslims would be equal, and condemned the religion.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r5.anchor: جمع أعمامه وقدم إليهم طعاما في صحفة فاستحقروه

RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r6.claim: A fourth report says Abu Lahab deterred visitors by calling the Prophet mad; when one delegation insisted on meeting him, Abu Lahab insulted him, the Prophet grieved, and the surah was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v32p152/r6.anchor: كان إذا وفد على النبي وفد سألوا عمه عنه

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r1.claim: One view takes tabbat to mean destruction; an old woman’s nickname and the verse about Pharaoh’s plot illustrate ruin.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r1.anchor: التباب الهلاك ، ومنه قولهم شابة أم تابة

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r2.claim: The Bedouin who had intercourse while fasting said he was ruined and had ruined his fast; since the Prophet did not deny him, Razi infers that abandoning a part of faith brings ruin, especially with Abu Lahab’s disbelief, speech, and actions.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r2.anchor: لما واقع أهله في نهار رمضان

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r3.claim: A second interpretation reads tabbat as loss that leads to destruction, as in the verse saying Pharaoh’s followers only increased him in loss.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r3.anchor: والتياب هو الخسران المفضي إلى الهلاك

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r4.claim: Tabbat may mean that Abu Lahab failed: he used his tribal authority to turn visitors away from the Prophet, but after the surah exposed his hostility, people distrusted him and his purpose failed.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لأنه كان يدفع القوم

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r5.claim: The mention of his hand may recall how he put it on visitors’ shoulders to push them away while calling the Prophet mad.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r5.anchor: كان يضرب بيده على كتف الوافد عليه

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r6.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation says tabbat means Abu Lahab was overcome, since he imagined his hand would prevail by expelling and humiliating the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r6.anchor: عن عطاء تبت أي غلبت لأنه كان يعتقد أن يده هي العليا

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r7.speaker: ابن وثاب
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r7.claim: Ibn Waththab explains the phrase as his hands being empty of every good.

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r8.claim: The hand may be singled out because Abu Lahab once took a stone intending to throw it at the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r8.anchor: ما يرى أنه أخذ حجرا ليرمي به رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r9.speaker: طارق المحاربي
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r9.claim: Tariq al-Muharibi reports seeing the Prophet preach in the market while a man stoned him and bloodied his heels; people identified the attacker as Abu Lahab, his uncle.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r9.anchor: طارق المحاربي أنه قال : رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r10.claim: Hands can stand for the whole person or all one’s deeds, as in Qur’anic expressions about what hands have sent ahead and what they made.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r10.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { ذالك بما قدمت يداك

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r11.claim: The two hands may signify his religion and worldly life, his beginning and end, or his capacities to acquire benefit and ward off harm.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r11.anchor: تبت يداه أي دينه ودنياه أولاه وعقباه

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet visited Abu Lahab at night to invite him to Islam; a speaking goat kid praised the Prophet, and Abu Lahab tore apart its hands in envy, prompting the curse.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r12.anchor: جئتني معتذرا فجلس النبي عليه السلام أمامه

RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r13.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r13.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Abu Lahab mocked the Prophet’s promises of posthumous events as unreal, then blew on his hands and wished them ruin; the surah came down.
RAZI-FULL:v32p153#2/r13.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق : يروى أن أبا لهب كان يقول

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r1.claim: The first wording may be a curse against Abu Lahab, like the Qur’anic curse on the human being who refuses to believe.

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r2.claim: Both clauses may be factual reports: the first says his work perished and the second that he himself perished, leaving him without either kind of benefit.

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r3.claim: Abu Muslim reads the first clause as the loss of Abu Lahab’s wealth and the second as his own ruin.

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the hands Abu Lahab himself and reads the second clause as his son Utbah’s ruin after he rejected the Prophet and was killed by a lion in Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r4.anchor: يعني نفسه : { وتب } يعني ولده عتبة

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r5.claim: The prediction can refer to Utbah’s later death because God already knew that it would occur.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r5.anchor: لأنه كان في معلومه تعالى أنه يحصل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r6.claim: The clauses may also mean that Abu Lahab failed to recognize his Lord’s right and then failed to recognize the Messenger’s right.

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r7.claim: The use of Abu Lahab’s kunya is not necessarily honorific: kunyas can function as names, as illustrated by readings and names such as Ali ibn Abu Talib.

RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r8.claim: Other explanations say the kunya became a proper name, replaced his birth name Abd al-Uzza, foretold his fiery end, or mocked his glowing cheeks.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154/r8.anchor: أنه كان اسمه عبد العزي فعدل عنه إلى كنيته

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s harsh address to his uncle is justified because Abu Lahab blocked the message by telling visitors Muhammad was mad; confronting him made his hostility public and his claims less credible.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r1.anchor: كان يصرف الناس عن محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r2.claim: Publicly confronting even his uncle showed that the Prophet would not compromise religious matters for anyone; if he would not spare his uncle, no one could expect favoritism.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r2.anchor: كان يداهن أحدا في الدين ويسامحه فيه

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r3.claim: Kinship would ordinarily call for compassion, but Abu Lahab’s severe enmity reversed that expectation and made severe treatment fitting.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r3.anchor: حصلت العداوة العظيمة ، لا جرم استحق التغليظ العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r4.claim: Unlike al-Kafirun, this surah does not command the Prophet to say the curse himself, sparing the respect due to his uncle’s kinship.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r4.anchor: رعاية الحرمة فلهذا السبب لم يقل له : قل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r5.claim: In al-Kafirun the unbelievers attacked God, so God told Muhammad to answer; here they attacked Muhammad, so God answered them Himself.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r5.anchor: طعنوا في الله فقال الله تعالى : يا محمد أجب عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r6.claim: The Prophet was to remain silent as the Qur’an instructs the servants of the Merciful to answer the ignorant peacefully, while God answered for him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r6.anchor: فاسكت حتى تندرج تحت هذه الآية : { وإذا خاطبهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r7.claim: A report says an angel defended Abu Bakr while he stayed silent, but withdrew when Abu Bakr began replying, when Satan came instead.
RAZI-FULL:v32p154#2/r7.anchor: حين كنت ساكتا كان الملك يجيب عنك

RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r1.claim: God defends, supports, and assists a person who does not directly answer a foolish or insulting speaker.
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r1.anchor: من لا يشافه السفيه كان الله ذابا عنه وناصرا له ومعينا

RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir of Mecca read Abu Lahab with a quiescent hā; Abu Ali explains Lahab and Lahb as dialect forms, though open hā is more eloquent in the other occurrences.
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r2.anchor: عبد الله بن كثير المكي حيث كان يقرأ

RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r3.claim: The readers all open the hā in the later occurrences, which suggests the open form is preferable; another explanation is that their opening preserves the rhyme.
RAZI-FULL:v32p155/r3.anchor: إنما اتفقوا على الفتح في الثانية مراعاة لو فاق الفواصل

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.claim: Al-Masad is considered one of the earliest Makkan surahs; its name comes from the final word, said to denote a Hell punishment, and it is also called al-Lahab, “The Flame.”
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r1.anchor: l-Masad is believed to be among the earliest Makkan

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.claim: Abū Lahab's nickname means “Father of Flame” and refers to his bright red complexion.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r2.anchor: known by the nickname Abū Lahab, “The Father of Flame,” because of his bright red complexion

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.claim: After the Prophet warned Quraysh from a hill, Abū Lahab cursed him for summoning them; God then revealed the five verses.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r3.anchor: Then God revealed the five verses

STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.speaker: many
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.claim: Many say the surah followed immediately after 26:214; its five short verses describe the Hell punishment of Abū Lahab and his wife.
STUDYQURAN:111:intro/r4.anchor: Many say this revelation occurred immediately after the revelation of 26:214

STUDYQURAN:111:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r1.claim: Abū Lahab was the wealthiest of the Prophet's uncles, a Quraysh leader who strongly opposed the Prophet and persecuted followers.
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r1.anchor: Abū Lahab was the wealthiest of the Prophet’s uncles and one of the Qurayshī leaders who most opposed the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:111:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r2.claim: “May his hands perish” is an idiom meaning that his power and possessions perish.
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r2.anchor: “May [his] hands perish” is an idiomatic expression meaning, “May his power perish and all that he possesses.”

STUDYQURAN:111:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r3.claim: Abū Lahab skipped Badr and reportedly died soon after from a festering wound inflicted by Umm al-Faḍl in retaliation for his abuse of her converted slave.
STUDYQURAN:111:1/r3.anchor: Abū Lahab did not go forth to the Battle of Badr, but is reported to have died soon thereafter

TAB:111:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r1.speaker: author
TAB:111:1/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Abū Lahab's hands and Abū Lahab himself have lost; the hands here signify his deeds.
TAB:111:1/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره : خسرت يدا أبي لهب ، وخسر هو . وإنما عني بقوله : { تبت يدا أبي لهب تب } عمله

TAB:111:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r2.speaker: نحوي
TAB:111:1/r2.claim: A grammarian reads the opening as God's imprecation against Abū Lahab.
TAB:111:1/r2.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول : قوله : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } : دعاء عليه من الله

TAB:111:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r3.speaker: author
TAB:111:1/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī treats the second clause, “and he has lost,” as a report of his ruin.

TAB:111:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB:111:1/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has “and he has indeed lost”; the added qad marks the clause as a report, not a curse.
TAB:111:1/r4.anchor: ويذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله : «تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب »

TAB:111:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r5.speaker: author
TAB:111:1/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains qad as showing reported fact through ordinary Arabic examples of a curse or wish followed by a statement that it has occurred.
TAB:111:1/r5.anchor: وفي دخول «قد » فيه دلالة على أنه خبر ، ويمثل ذلك بقول القائل لآخر : أهلكك الله ، وقد أهلكك

TAB:111:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:111:1/r6.claim: Qatāda glosses the opening as loss and ruin.
TAB:111:1/r6.anchor: عن قتادة { تبت يدا أبي لهب } : أي خسرت وتب

TAB:111:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:111:1/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd explains tabba as loss and reports that Abū Lahab rejected Islam because he would receive no privilege over other Muslims.
TAB:111:1/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد ، في قول الله : { تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب } قال : التب : الخسران

TAB:111:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:111:1/r8.claim: Qatāda also paraphrases the verse as Abū Lahab's hands and himself having lost.
TAB:111:1/r8.anchor: عن قتادة { تبت يدا أبي لهب } قال : خسرت يدا أبي لهب وخسر

TAB:111:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r9.speaker: author
TAB:111:1/r9.claim: The surah was revealed after the Prophet warned his nearest relatives, as commanded in 26:214, and Abū Lahab cursed him for summoning them.
TAB:111:1/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن هذه السورة نزلت في أبي لهب ؛ لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما خص بالدعوة عشيرته ، إذ نزل عليه : { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } وجمعهم للدعاء

TAB:111:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:111:1/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after the Prophet called the Quraysh together on Ṣafā and warned of severe punishment, Abū Lahab cursed him; the surah was revealed.
TAB:111:1/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم الصفا ، فقال : «يا صباحاه » ، فاجتمعت إليه قريش

TAB:111:1/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:111:1/r11.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report expands the warning to the Prophet's clans and the hypothetical approaching cavalry; the crowd affirmed his truthfulness before Abū Lahab's curse and the revelation.
TAB:111:1/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : لما نزلت { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصفا

TAB:111:1/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:111:1/r12.claim: In another narration read by al-Aʿmash, the Prophet's warning to his relatives follows 26:214, and Abū Lahab's reply precedes the reading tabbat yadā Abī Lahab wa-qad tabb.
TAB:111:1/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية : ( { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } ورهطك منهم المخلصين ) ، خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB:111:1/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:111:1/r13.speaker: سفيان
TAB:111:1/r13.claim: Sufyān says Abū Lahab was the Prophet's paternal uncle, named ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, and cursed him when the Prophet summoned him and others.
TAB:111:1/r13.anchor: عن سفيان ، في قوله : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } قال : حين أرسل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إليه وإلى غيره ، وكان أبو لهب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r1.claim: He glosses tabbat as loss and links the root to the earlier discussion of tabāb in Ghāfir.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r1.anchor: أي: خسرت، وتقدم تفسير هذه المادة

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r2.claim: The hands stand metonymically for the whole person, since most actions are done with them; the wording moves from a part to the whole.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r2.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى اليدين مجازا لأن أكثر الأفعال تزاول بهما

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r3.speaker: author
