SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r3.claim: Initially, tabbat is a curse or prayer and tab reports its fulfillment; he then says the apparent reading makes both verbs prayers.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r3.anchor: وقوله: " تبت " دعاء، و " تب " إخبار، أي: قد وقع

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r4.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r4.claim: His reading وقد تب supports taking the second verb as reporting that the curse came to pass.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r4.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة عبد الله " وقد تب " والظاهر أن كليهما دعاء

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r5.claim: Most readers open the hāʾ of Lahab, while Ibn Kathīr sukunizes it; one view treats both forms as dialect variants, like النهر and الشعر.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة " لهب " بفتح الهاء. وابن كثير بإسكانها. فقيل: لغتان بمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r6.claim: He explains the altered vowel in the proper name by analogy with Shams ibn Mālik, whose name is said to have changed from fatḥa to ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وهو من تغيير الأعلام كقوله: " شمس ابن مالك

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r7.claim: The shams example need not involve a changed proper name: shams can be the plural form attested in a phrase about horses.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r7.anchor: وجوز الشيخ في " شمس " أن يكون منقولا من " شمس " الجمع من قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r8.claim: The kunya Abū Lahab may allude to his flushed, inflamed cheeks, his eventual Hellfire, its greater fame, the status of a kunya, or the ugliness of his given name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r8.anchor: وكنى بذلك: إما لالتهاب وجنتيه، وكان مشرق الوجه أحمره، وإما لما يؤول

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r9.claim: He gives three reasons for using a kunya: it was famous, his given name was ugly, or he was destined for Hellfire.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر ثلاثة أجوبة: إما لشهرته بكنيته، وإما لقبح اسمه كما تقدم، وإما لأن مآله

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r10.claim: The claim that the kunya is less complete conflicts with the later claim that a kunya is more honorable and complete.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r10.anchor: انتهى. وهذا يقتضي أن الكنية أشرف وأكمل لا أنقص، وهو عكس قول تقدم آنفا.

SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r11.claim: A reading puts Abū in the nominative to preserve the name unchanged, as in familiar names and a reported distinction between two men named ʿAbd Allāh.
SAMIN-DURR:111:1/r11.anchor: وقرئ: " يدا أبو لهب " بالواو في مكان الجر. قال الزمخشري:

ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r1.claim: Tabbat yadā means Abū Lahab's hands were ruined or lost.
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r1.anchor: معناه خسرت يدا أبي لهب، وتب: أي خسر.

ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r2.claim: Tafsir recounts that the Prophet invited his uncles to a meal that miraculously fed them with almost no food missing; when they asked what following him would bring, he said equal Muslim duties and reward, and Abū Lahab cursed him, prompting the sura.
ZAJJAJ:v5p375/r2.anchor: فأكلوا منها جميعا ولم ينقص منها إلا الشيء اليسير، فقالوا: مالنا عندك إن اتبعناك،

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r1.claim: The Meccan sura threatens Abu Lahab, his deeds, and his wife with destruction and Hell.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد شديد لأبي لهب بهلاك نفسه وعمله وبنار جهنم ولامرأته، والسورة مكية

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r2.speaker: الجوهري
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r2.claim: Al-Jawhari explains tabab as loss and destruction; al-Raghib adds enduring loss, while others gloss it as disappointment or total lack of good.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r2.anchor: التب والتباب هو الخسران والهلاك على ما ذكره الجوهري، ودوام الخسران على ما ذكره الراغب

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r3.claim: The hands stand for means of achieving aims; their ruin means failed deeds, especially Abu Lahab's efforts to extinguish prophethood, and his own lasting loss of felicity.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r3.anchor: وتباب يديه خسرانهما فيما تكتسبانه من عمل وإن شئت فقل بطلان أعماله

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r4.claim: The opening may be a curse against Abu Lahab's self and deeds, or God's decree that he be ruined.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r4.anchor: دعاء عليه بهلاك نفسه وبطلان ما كان يأتيه من الأعمال لإطفاء نور النبوة أو قضاء منه تعالى بذلك

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r5.claim: Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle, was persistently hostile and abusive; after the first public invitation he told the Prophet to perish, and this sura answered him.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r5.anchor: كان شديد المعاداة للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مصرا في تكذيبه مبالغا في إيذائه

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r6.claim: Some say Abu Lahab was his given name despite its form as a kunya; other reported names are Abd al-Uzza and Abd Manaf.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r6.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن أبا لهب اسمه وإن كان في صورة الكنية، وقيل اسمه عبد العزى وقيل عبد مناف

TABATABAI:111:1-4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r7.claim: The kunya is preferable to his personal name because Abu Lahab mocks him as bound to Hell's flames; Abd al-Uzza was avoided because al-Uzza is an idol's name.
TABATABAI:111:1-4/r7.anchor: في ذكره في الآية بكنيته لا باسمه أن في ذلك تهكما به لأن أبا لهب يشعر بالنسبة إلى لهب النار

TABATABAI:111:5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r3.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:111:5/r3.claim: Al-Majma' asks whether Abu Lahab was still obligated to believe and could have done so without disproving the threat; it answers that faith remained obligatory and the threat was conditional on disbelief.
TABATABAI:111:5/r3.anchor: فالجواب أن الإيمان يلزمه لأن تكليف الإيمان ثابت عليه وإنما توعده الله بشرط أن لا يؤمن

TABATABAI:111:5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:5/r4.claim: The author says God's decisive decree does not cancel choice: He wills human acts as voluntary, so Abu Lahab could choose faith and escape the punishment decreed for his unbelief.
TABATABAI:111:5/r4.anchor: أن تعلق القضاء الحتمي منه تعالى بفعل الإنسان الاختياري لا يستوجب بطلان الاختيار

TABATABAI:111:5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:5/r5.claim: The same pattern applies to declarations that Quraysh disbelievers will not believe and to verses about hearts being sealed.
TABATABAI:111:5/r5.anchor: ومن هذا الباب الآيات النازلة في كفار قريش أنهم لا يؤمنون

TABATABAI:111:5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:111:5/r6.claim: After the warning to nearest kin, the Prophet asked Quraysh whether they would believe a warning of imminent attack; when they affirmed, he warned them of punishment and Abu Lahab cursed him, prompting the sura.
TABATABAI:111:5/r6.anchor: قال أبو لهب تبا لك ألهذا دعوتنا جميعا؟ فأنزل الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:111:5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:111:5/r7.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says Sa'id ibn Jubayr also transmits the Ibn Abbas account in the sura commentary, without linking it to the nearest-kin verse.
TABATABAI:111:5/r7.anchor: ورواه أيضا في تفسير السورة عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:111:5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:5/r8.speaker: طارق المحاربي
TABATABAI:111:5/r8.claim: At the Dhul-Majaz market, he saw Muhammad inviting people to profess God's unity while Abu Lahab followed, bleeding his legs and calling him a liar.
TABATABAI:111:5/r8.anchor: إذا أنا بشاب يقول أيها الناس قولوا لا إله إلا الله تفلحوا، وإذا برجل خلفه يرميه

TABATABAI:111:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r1.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r1.claim: When the sura was revealed, Umm Jamil approached angrily with a stone; the Prophet told Abu Bakr she could not see him, and said God had placed a barrier between them.
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r1.anchor: أن أم جميل امرأه أبي لهب أتته حين نزلت سورة تبت ومع النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أبو بكر

TABATABAI:111:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r2.claim: Comparable versions of the Umm Jamil account occur through several Sunni chains.
TABATABAI:111:1-5/r2.anchor: وروي ما يقرب منه بغير واحد من طرق أهل السنة

TABRISI:111:3-5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-5/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:111:3-5/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the hāʾ in Abu Lahab with sukūn; the other readers pronounce it with fatḥ.
TABRISI:111:3-5/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير أبي لهب ساكنة الهاء والباقي بفتحها

TABRISI:111:3-5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-5/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:111:3-5/r6.claim: Abu Ali treats Lahab and Lahab as dialect forms like al-shamʿ and al-nahr; the unanimous fatḥ in “dhāt lahab” supports that vocalization.
TABRISI:111:3-5/r6.anchor: يشبه أن يكون لهب ولهب لغتين كالشمع والشمع والنهر والنهر

TABRISI:111:3-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-5/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:111:3-5/r12.claim: The root tabb and the noun tabāb mean ruin that leads to destruction; masad is rope made of palm fiber, with amsād as its plural, as a cited poem shows.
TABRISI:111:3-5/r12.anchor: التب والتباب الخسران المؤدي إلى الهلاك والمسد الحبل من الليف وجمعه أمساد

TABRISI:111:3-4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:111:3-4/r1.claim: Abu Lahab curses Muhammad after the Safa warning; the surah is then revealed, and al-Bukhari includes the report in his Sahih.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r1.anchor: فقال أبو لهب: تبا لك لهذا دعوتنا جميعا فأنزل الله هذه السورة

TABRISI:111:3-4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r2.claim: Muqatil explains “perished are Abu Lahab's hands” as his hands and he himself being ruined; hands stand for work because most work is done by them, and the ultimate loss is his soul in the Fire.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل وإنما قال خسرت يداه لأن أكثر العمل يكون باليد والمراد خسر عمله

TABRISI:111:3-4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r3.claim: An alternative takes “hand” as an auxiliary expression, like “the hand of time” or “the hand of the year,” with a cited poem as evidence.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r3.anchor: إن اليد هنا صلة كقولهم يد الدهر ويد السنة

TABRISI:111:3-4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r4.claim: Another interpretation says Abu Lahab's hands were emptied of every good; al-Farraʾ reads the first phrase as a curse and the second as a report that he has perished.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: الأول دعاء والثاني خبر فكأنه قال أهلكه الله

TABRISI:111:3-4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r5.claim: A further view treats both phrases as reports: his hands never earned good, and he himself was ruined as well; the verse says he perished in every respect.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن الأول أيضا خبر ومعناه أنه لم تكتسب يداه خيرا قط

TABRISI:111:3-4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:111:3-4/r6.claim: Abu Lahab is Muhammad's paternal uncle, known for intense hostility and opposition; Tariq al-Muharibi recounts seeing him follow Muhammad at Dhu al-Majaz and call him a liar.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r6.anchor: وأبو لهب هو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان شديد المعاداة

TABRISI:111:3-4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r7.speaker: طارق المحاربي
TABRISI:111:3-4/r7.claim: Tariq al-Muharibi reports that people identified Muhammad as a prophet and Abu Lahab as his uncle who called him a liar while following him and injuring his legs.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r7.anchor: قال طارق المحاربي: بينا أنا بسوق ذي المجاز إذا أنا بشاب

TABRISI:111:3-4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:111:3-4/r8.claim: One explanation says God uses Abu Lahab's familiar epithet because it was more commonly used than his personal name.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r8.anchor: وإنما ذكر سبحانه كنيته دون اسمه لأنها كانت أغلب عليه

TABRISI:111:3-4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r9.claim: Another explanation avoids calling him Abd al-Uzza, since he is God's servant rather than a servant of al-Uzza.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r9.anchor: لأن اسمه عبد العزى فكره الله سبحانه أن ينسبه إلى العزى

TABRISI:111:3-4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:111:3-4/r10.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:111:3-4/r10.claim: Muqatil says Abu Lahab was so named for his beauty and bright face, with cheeks that seemed to flame.
TABRISI:111:3-4/r10.anchor: وكانت وجنتاه كأنهما تلتهبان عن مقاتل

THALABI:v10p323#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p323#3/r1.claim: When the Prophet warned his closest relatives at Safa that a severe punishment was coming, Abu Lahab cursed him for summoning them; the verse then declared Abu Lahab ruined.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أنزل الله سبحانه: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفا

THALABI:v10p323#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p323#3/r2.claim: Tabbat means she failed and lost; hands refer to the whole person by the Arabs' practice of using a part for the whole.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r2.anchor: فأنزل تبت أي خابت وخسرت، يدا أبي لهب أي تب هو أخبر عن يديه والمراد به نفسه

THALABI:v10p323#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p323#3/r3.claim: Another explanation treats yad as an idiom or appendage, as in Arabs' expressions hand of time and hand of calamities.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: اليد صلة يقول العرب: يد الدهر ويد الرزايا والمنايا،

THALABI:v10p323#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p323#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the hands mean his money and property; the expression little in hand means little wealth.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد به ماله وملكه يقال: فلان قليل ذات اليد،

THALABI:v10p323#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
THALABI:v10p323#3/r5.claim: A report says that after Uthman was killed, people heard a jinn voice lamenting those who had deserted him and failed to return.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r5.anchor: عن الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء قال: لما قتل عثمان رضي الله عنه سمعوا صوت هاتف

THALABI:v10p323#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p323#3/r6.claim: Abu Lahab was the son of Abd al-Muttalib, named Abd al-Uzza, so the sura does not use his pagan given name; another says he was named Kuthayba, and Muqatil connects the nickname to his glowing beauty.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r6.anchor: وأبو لهب هو ابن عبد المطلب واسمه عبد العزي فلذلك لم يسمه، وقيل اسمه كتيبة

THALABI:v10p323#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p323#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p323#3/r7.claim: The conjunction waw connects the two clauses; Ibn Masud and Ubayy read qad tabba, making the first clause a curse and the second its confirmation, with waw also explained as circumstantial.
THALABI:v10p323#3/r7.anchor: وتب أبو لهب الواو فيه واو العطف، وقرأ عبد الله وأبي (وقد تب) فالأول دعاء

THALABI:v10p324/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p324/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p324/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when God created the Pen and ordered it to write what would occur, it wrote that Abu Lahab's hands would perish.
THALABI:v10p324/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما خلق الله القلم قال: أكتب ما هو كائن فكتب فمما كتب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and the commentators report that after the Prophet summoned Quraysh at Ṣafā and warned of an approaching punishment, Abū Lahab cursed him for gathering them; the sūra was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (في رواية سعيد بن جبير) (¬4) (¬5) وجماعة # المفسرين (¬1): صعد رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ذات يوم: الصفا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r2.claim: The opening means Abū Lahab’s hands were ruined and he himself was ruined; this is the general interpretation, with a parallel phrase cited from Ghāfir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r2.anchor: أي خسرت يدا أبي لهب، وخسر هو، (وهذا قول عامتهم) (¬2) (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says his hands were ruined by abandoning faith, and he himself was ruined.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: خسرت يداه (¬2) بترك الإيمان، وخسر هو (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses the first “perished” as a prayer and the second as a report, like praying God destroy someone and then saying he perished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: الأول: دعاء (¬4)، والثاني: خبر، كما تقول: أهلكه الله وقد هلك (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r5.claim: Attributing loss to the hand is an idiom for its owner, like saying someone’s hand lost, narrowed, or earned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r5.anchor: وأضاف التباب إلى اليد كقول العرب: خسرت يده وضاقت يده، وكسبت يده، والمراد به صاحب اليد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r6.claim: Abū Lahab was the Prophet’s uncle, son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; he is named by his epithet rather than the improper ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, and was intensely hostile to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r6.anchor: وأبو لهب هو ابن عبد المطلب -عم النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- واسمه عبد العزى، ولهذا ذكرت كنيته دون اسمه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r7.speaker: طاوس بن عبد الله المحاربي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r7.claim: Ṭāwūs ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muḥāribī recounts seeing Muhammad call people to the testimony at Dhū al-Majāz while Abū Lahab followed, bloodied his legs, and called him a liar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r7.anchor: قال طاوس بن عبد الله (المحاربي) (¬9): أتى بسوق ذي # المجاز (¬1) (¬2)؛ إذا أنا بشاب يقول: يا أيها (¬3) الناس قولوا: لا إله إلا الله تفلحوا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r8.speaker: أبو الضحى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r8.claim: Abū al-Ḍuḥā says he was called Abū Lahab for his handsome, glowing appearance; Ibn Kathīr of Mecca read the hāʾ in lahb with sukūn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p407#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو الضحى: إنما كني باللهب لحسنه، وكان يتلهب من حسنه (¬6) وهو قول عبد الله ابن كثير المكي القاري، وكان يقرأ (أبي لهب) ساكنة الهاء

WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r1.claim: After the command to warn his close kin, the Prophet called people from al-Safa, warned them of the Fire, and Abu Lahab cursed him; this occasioned the surah.
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r1.anchor: نادى بأعلى صوته يدعو قومه فاجتمعوا إليه

WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r2.claim: “Perished” means Abu Lahab's hands failed and he himself was ruined.
WAHIDI-QT:111:1/r2.anchor: أي خابت وخسرت { وتب } وخسر هو

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r1.claim: After the command to warn his near relatives, the Prophet called Quraysh from Safa, gathered them, warned of the Fire, and Abu Lahab cursed him for summoning them; this occasion led to the sura's revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r1.anchor: لما نزل قوله: { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفا، ونادى بأعلى صوته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r2.claim: The opening means Abu Lahab's hands failed and lost, and he himself failed and lost.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:111:1-5/r2.anchor: تبت يدا أبي لهب } أي: خابت وخسرت { وتب } وخسر هو،

ASAD-NOTES:111:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:111:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:111:intro/r1.claim: This very early Meccan surah, sixth in revelation order, takes its name from its final word and addresses Abu Lahab’s hostility, rooted in arrogance, wealth, and resistance to human equality and judgment by merit; Ibn Zayd is cited by Tabari.
ASAD-NOTES:111:intro/r1.anchor: arrogance, pride in his great wealth

ASAD-NOTES:111:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:111:1/r1.speaker: Baghawi; Muqatil; Zamakhshari; Razi
ASAD-NOTES:111:1/r1.claim: Abu Lahab’s nickname meant “He of the Flame” and referred to his handsome, glowing face; because it predated Islam, Asad says it was not pejorative.

ASAD-NOTES:111:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:111:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:111:1#n1/r1.claim: Abu Lahab’s real name was Abd al-Uzza.
ASAD-NOTES:111:1#n1/r1.anchor: The real name of this uncle of the Prophet was Abd al-Uzza.

ELMALILI:111:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r1.claim: Tabbat is formally informative but can perform loss as a curse or as an enacted divine ruin; the curse also conveys blame and condemnation.
ELMALILI:111:1/r1.anchor: tebâb oldu bu fiil esasen ihbâra mevzû‘olmakla beraber ibare

ELMALILI:111:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r2.claim: Many interpreters of the first revelation took the phrase as an imprecation, hence the common rendering “may his hands wither.”
ELMALILI:111:1/r2.anchor: İlk nüzûle nazaran çokları bu mânaya haml eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:111:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r3.claim: “May his hand wither” first suggests paralysis, but figuratively asks that he be bankrupt, powerless, and frustrated in every effort.
ELMALILI:111:1/r3.anchor: “Eli kurusun” tâbiri daha ziyade شَلَّتْ يَدُهُ

ELMALILI:111:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r4.claim: “May he be ruined” or “ruined he was” better captures tabāb; Abu Lahab’s later confirmed ruin makes the declarative sense especially apt.
ELMALILI:111:1/r4.anchor: Bunu “yuf olsun, yuha gitsin, berbat olsun” diye ifade etmek

ELMALILI:111:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r5.claim: The surah’s placement after the Prophet’s victory and Abu Lahab’s death signals fulfilled foretelling: his ruin only deepened, while the wording still condemns him.
ELMALILI:111:1/r5.anchor: bu sûrenin tertibde buraya konulması bunda ihbar mânası maksud olduğuna

ELMALILI:111:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r6.claim: His two hands stand for every means he tried to use, for or against, in worldly and religious affairs; all his efforts against the Prophet and Islam turned against him.
ELMALILI:111:1/r6.anchor: gerek müsbet gerek menfî, gerek tutmak gerek itmek için kullanmak istediği

ELMALILI:111:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r7.claim: Abu Lahab is singled out between the surahs about the Prophet and God despite other unnamed enemies; this marks him out among the criminals, echoing Yasin.
ELMALILI:111:1/r7.anchor: Ona وَٱمْتَٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ [Yâsin 36/59] mazmûnu üzere

ELMALILI:111:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r8.claim: His special distinction is more lamentable because he was the Prophet’s paternal uncle yet opposed him; the contrast exalts the Prophet and divine truth above lineage.
ELMALILI:111:1/r8.anchor: Çünkü Ebû Leheb Peygamber’in baba bir amcası olmak haysiyetiyle

ELMALILI:111:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r9.claim: The epithet “Abu Lahab,” literally father of flame, represents fire-spewing enemies of Islam, so his ruin exemplifies theirs and points to God completing His light.
ELMALILI:111:1/r9.anchor: “Ebû Leheb” şahsı gösteren bir künye olmakla beraber lügaten

ELMALILI:111:1/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r10.claim: Kunyas can denote a characteristic as well as a person’s name; Abu Lahab therefore alludes to being hell-bound without ceasing to refer to the historical man.
ELMALILI:111:1/r10.anchor: kinayeler hakikatin iradesine mâni‘olmayacağına binâen burada bu mânanın ehemmiyet-i mahsûsası

ELMALILI:111:1/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r11.claim: His given name was Abd al-Uzza; his red cheeks brought the fire-associated kunya, initially suggesting brightness, fiery temperament, or severity.
ELMALILI:111:1/r11.anchor: Onun asıl ismi Abdüluzzâ b. Abdülmuttalib iken yanakları pek kırmızı olduğu için

ELMALILI:111:1/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r12.claim: The kunya’s real implication became his conduct: by choosing hostility and refusing faith, he made himself a source and lover of fire, a model of hell’s people.
ELMALILI:111:1/r12.anchor: bunun hakikatinde bir ateş kaynağı olmak veya ateşi sevmek mânası bulunduğu

ELMALILI:111:1/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r13.claim: Despite his kinship and status, he persisted in hostility; his fate should make other unrepentant enemies of the Prophet consider their own ruin.
ELMALILI:111:1/r13.anchor: Peygamber’e buğzedip de tevbe etmeyen diğerlerinin ne kadar ebter ve bedbaht olacakları

ELMALILI:111:1/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r14.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:111:1/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives three reasons for the honorific kunya: Abu Lahab was known by it, it avoids his name Abd al-Uzza, and it suits a person of the Fire.
ELMALILI:111:1/r14.anchor: Keşşâf’ta der ki: “Tekniye tekrim ifade ederken burada künye ile anılmasında

ELMALILI:111:1/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r15.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:111:1/r15.claim: One explanation is that Abu Lahab was simply famous by his kunya rather than by his personal name.

ELMALILI:111:1/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r16.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:111:1/r16.claim: A second explanation is that the text avoids his personal name, Abd al-Uzza.
ELMALILI:111:1/r16.anchor: ikincisi ismi Abdüluzzâ olduğu için ondan udûl olunmuştur

ELMALILI:111:1/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r17.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:111:1/r17.claim: A third explanation is that the kunya suits him as one of the people of Hell; the pattern also names an evil person Abu al-Sharr.
ELMALILI:111:1/r17.anchor: Üçüncüsü meâli نَارًۭا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍۢ olan ehl-i nârdan olduğu için künyesi

ELMALILI:111:1/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r18.claim: “And he was ruined” separately states that Abu Lahab himself failed, missed his aim, and perished in loss.
ELMALILI:111:1/r18.anchor: Evet, Ebû Leheb’in iki eli yuha, hüsrana gitti, tebâb oldu

ELMALILI:111:1/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r19.claim: Abu Lahab supported Quraysh financially at Badr but could not attend because of illness, sending As ibn Hisham, Abu Jahl’s brother, in his place.
ELMALILI:111:1/r19.anchor: hastalığından dolayı Bedir’e bizzat iştirak edememiş, fakat mâlen yardım ederek

ELMALILI:111:1/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r20.claim: He contracted adasa, described as a smallpox-like illness, and died from grief seven days after learning Quraysh had been defeated at Badr.
ELMALILI:111:1/r20.anchor: Kendisi “adese” denilen çiçek kabîlinden bir illete tutulmuş

ELMALILI:111:1/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r21.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:111:1/r21.claim: Al-Alusi and others say Quraysh feared adasa like plague; even his family stayed away, and his corpse lay for three days and smelled.
ELMALILI:111:1/r21.anchor: Âlûsî ve daha sâirlerinin de naklettiği vechile Kureyş adeseden tâun gibi sakındıkları

ELMALILI:111:1/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r22.claim: One burial account says hired Sudanese carried him, dug a pit, placed him inside with wood, and covered him with stones.
ELMALILI:111:1/r22.anchor: bir çukur kazıp ağaçlarla içine kakmışlar, örtünceye kadar da üzerine taş atmışlar

ELMALILI:111:1/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r23.claim: Another burial account says they dug no pit, propped the corpse beside a wall, and threw stones until it was covered.
ELMALILI:111:1/r23.anchor: diğer bir rivayette çukur da kazmamışlar, bir duvarın dibine dayayıp

ELMALILI:111:1/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:1/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:1/r24.claim: The predicted earthly death came about about fifteen years after the revelation, but the verse means enduring bodily and spiritual loss through afterlife punishment too.
ELMALILI:111:1/r24.anchor: ma‘amâfîh murad, sade böyle oluşundan ibaret değil, dünyada maksadına

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.claim: The opening prediction was fulfilled: because Abu Lahab did not believe in God’s oneness, he could not benefit from the Prophet’s intercession; status and wealth did not rescue him.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r15.anchor: Tâ risâletin bidâyetinde haber verilmiş olan bu hakikat böylece tahakkuk etmiş

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.claim: He did not repent of saying “tabban lak”; he died in ruin, and the author seeks refuge from an evil ending.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r16.anchor: ona تـَبًّا لَك dediğine tevbe de nasib olmayıp böyle tebâb olmuş gitmiştir

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.claim: After contrasting the good and ruined endings, the text points to monotheism and sincerity, then refuge in God, as the path to a good end.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r17.anchor: Şimdi biri, tesbih ve hamd ve istiğfar ile Allah’a giden, biri de hüsran

ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.claim: The conclusion prepares for Ikhlas by saying that knowing God through pure monotheism and seeking His protection is the remedy for ruin.
ELMALILI:111:2-5#2/r18.anchor: Allah târif edilerek tevhid ve ihlâs ile O’na ilticâ emrolunacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r1.claim: Abu Lahab was Abd al-Muttalib's son and the Prophet's paternal uncle; his nickname means flame-like or very bright, because of his face or reddening cheeks when angry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r1.anchor: Abdülmuttalib’in oğlu ve Hz. Peygamber’in baba bir amcasıdır. Asıl adı Abdülüzzâ olup parlak yüzlü olduğundan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r2.claim: Though formerly fond of Muhammad and having married two sons to his daughters, Abu Lahab became a fierce enemy after the prophethood began.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r2.anchor: Daha önce Hz. Muhammed’i çok sevdiği, hatta iki oğlunu onun kızlarıyla evlendirdiği halde peygamber olduktan sonra onun azılı düşmanı oldu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r3.claim: The Prophet taught that people are equal before God and judged by religious and moral virtue; proud, wealthy Abu Lahab could not accept the equality of poor and weak people with himself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r3.anchor: Ebû Leheb ise kibirli, gururlu ve zengin biri olup fakir ve zayıf insanların kendisine eşit tutulmasını kabullenemiyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r4.claim: A report says Abu Lahab followed the Prophet through the market as he preached and told people around him that the Prophet was a liar.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r4.anchor: Resûlullah panayırda dolaşarak insanları İslâm’a davet ederken Ebû Leheb de arkasından gider ve çevresindekilere onun yalancı olduğunu söylerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r5.claim: Abu Lahab and his wife constantly joined the Prophet's enemies and caused him harm.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r5.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’e karşı daima onun düşmanlarıyla birlikte hareket etmiş, hem kendisi hem de karısı ona eziyet etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.claim: In year two of the Hijra Abu Lahab contracted smallpox and could not attend Badr, but sent a replacement and financially supported the polytheists; he reportedly died of grief seven days after their defeat.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r6.anchor: çiçek hastalığına yakalandığı için müslümanlara karşı Bedir Savaşı’na katılamamış, fakat yerine adam göndermiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r7.claim: Fearing contagion, his family reportedly stayed away after his death and hired Sudanese men to bury him; his daughter later became Muslim and emigrated, and two sons converted after Mecca's conquest.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r7.anchor: öldüğünde ücretle tuttukları Sudanlılar’a defnettirdikleri rivayet edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r8.claim: The first verse's image of Abu Lahab's hands perishing is a figurative imprecation meaning damnation; the following verb predicts its fulfillment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r8.anchor: “Ebû Leheb’in elleri kurusun!” meâlindeki 1. âyet mecazi bir ifade olup, “Kahrolası!” anlamında bir bedduadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r9.claim: A common figurative reading is that his work and affairs should fail; some distinguish the first curse as loss in his affairs and the second as news of his personal ruin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:111:1/r9.anchor: İlk “kuruma”yı işlerinin kötü gitmesi için beddua, ikinci “kuruma”yı ise kendi şahsının (nefs) perişan olduğu yönünde bir haber

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r1.claim: On Safa the Prophet called Quraysh, asked if they would believe his warning of an approaching enemy, and warned of severe punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him and the surah was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم على الصفا فنادى يا صباحاه فاجتمعت إليه قريش

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r2.speaker: يزيد بن زيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r2.claim: A report through Ibn Ishaq says Abu Lahab's wife used to place thorns in the Prophet's path, and the surah from its opening through the verse about his wife was revealed; Ikrima reports similarly.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p237#2/r2.anchor: عن رجل من همدان يقال له يزيد بن زيد أن امراة أبي ليست كانت تلقي في طريق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشوك فنزلت

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r1.claim: The Prophet called Quraysh from Safa and asked whether they would believe his warning of an approaching enemy; when he warned of severe punishment, Abu Lahab cursed him and the surah was revealed. Al-Bukhari also transmits this account.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: صعد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذات يوم الصفا فقال:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the Prophet summoned the clans and said he could offer no protection or worldly share, only the call to God's oneness; Abu Lahab cursed him and the verse followed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r3.claim: A further Ibn Abbas account connects the revelation to 26:214: after calling his nearest kin at Safa and warning that enemy cavalry might attack, Abu Lahab cursed him and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p469/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أنزل الله تعالى: {وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين} (1) أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الصفا

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r1.claim: The construction ʾabū plus genitive marks a person by a defining trait, as in “father of guests”; plural aṣḥāb plus genitive works similarly, for example in 85:4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Verbindung ʾabū + Substantiv im Genitiv dient dazu, jemanden als Besitzer einer bestimmten Eigentümlichkeit zu charakterisieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Horovitz
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r2.claim: Horovitz suggests “Father of Flame” is not an actual name but a figurative kunya coined by the sura to mark its bearer as hellbound.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Horovitz vermutet, dass die Wendung „Vater der Flamme“ (ʾabū lahab) „kein eigentlicher Name“ sei

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r3.claim: If the figure is Muhammad’s uncle ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, his “Father of Flame” epithet likely arose after this sura; the phrase should be translated to retain its link to the fire imagery in verse 3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r3.anchor: so dürfte der Beiname „Vater der Flamme“ ihm erst im Gefolge der vorliegenden Koransure beigelegt worden sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r4.claim: The sura may instead describe a generic archetypal damned man of flames, like the wretched one burning in 92:15; identifying him with ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā may be a later anecdotal development in early Quran reception.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Keineswegs auszuschließen ist allerdings, dass sich die Sure ursprünglich gar nicht gegen eine bestimmte Einzelperson richtet

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Rubin
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r5.claim: Rubin takes yad as merit, translating the line as Abū Lahab’s merits being lost, based on a report that ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā earned merit through a vow to tend al-ʿUzzā’s shrine.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Rubin, der die Sure primär im Rückgriff auf außerkoranische Traditionen deutet, will yad im Sinne von „Verdienst“ verstehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r6.claim: Although yad can mean merit, Fischer’s synecdoche of Abū Lahab’s two hands for his whole person is more likely, since the dual fits poorly with an abstract meaning.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r6.anchor: doch ist August Fischers Verständnis der beiden Hände von ʾabū lahab“ als einer Synekdoche für die gesamte Person des Verfluchten wahrscheinlicher

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r7.claim: The objection that repeating tabba makes the hands and the person distinct fails: the final phrase most likely emphatically repeats the curse.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Das den Vers abschließende wa-tabba ist am ehesten als eine bekräftigende Wiederholung der vorangehenden Verwünschung aufzufassen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r8.claim: Classical exegetes gloss tabba as either losing or perishing; Rubin sees “lose” as original and “perish” as secondary overlay, but that depends on his reading yad as merit.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Das Verb tabba selbst wird von islamischen Exegeten sowohl mit ḫasira

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r9.claim: With Fischer’s synecdoche, both glosses are possible nuances rather than competing meanings.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r9.anchor: es handelt sich bei den beiden Glossen deshalb wohl eher um unterschiedliche semantische Nuancen

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r10.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r10.claim: The reported reading wa-qad tabba by Ibn Masʿūd, al-Aʿmaš, and Ubayy b. Kaʿb clarifies the ambiguous text secondarily; the received wa-tabba is the more difficult reading and should stand.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r10.anchor: Von Ibn Masʿūd, al-Aʿmaš und Ubayy b. Kaʿb wird die Lesart wa-qad tabba überliefert

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r11.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r11.speaker: Fischer
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r11.claim: Fischer reads the second tabba as a past assertion that doom has already struck, intensifying the preceding curse; Paret instead favors emphatic repetition, comparable to qutila in 74:19–20.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1:anmerkung/r11.anchor: August Fischer übersetzt das zweite tabba nicht als Imprekativ

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops from a curse against an enemy called ‘Father of Flame’; all verses except verse 5 refer back to him pronominally.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:1-2:kommentar/r1.anchor: Der Text entwickelt sich aus der einleitenden Verwünschung eines als „Vater der Flammen“ bezeichneten Gegners heraus

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r2.claim: Following Neuwirth’s observation, the pointed name Abū Lahab is only fully articulated by verse 3’s nār ḏāt lahab; the fire scene retrospectively motivates ‘Father of Flame.’
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die zentrale sprachliche Pointe des Textes besteht darin, dass

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r3.claim: The text first leaves Abū Lahab enigmatic, then motivates the name through the hellfire description, creating rhetorical tension.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r3.anchor: die zunächst änigmatische Bezeichnung ʾabū lahab, „Vater der Flamme“, wird also durch die Höllenbeschreibung in V. 3

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r1.speaker: Imām Ḥamīd Uddin Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r1.claim: Farāhī says the conquest completed the Prophet's mission and the Qur'an ends with that victory; the Kaʿbah is the center of Abraham's monotheistic religion, followed by sūrahs of monotheism and protection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r1.anchor: My mentor Im ām Ḥam īd Uddin Far āhī has dealt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r2.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r2.claim: Farāhī says al-Naṣr, al-Ikhlāṣ, and the two refuge sūrahs form a harmonious sequence, so al-Lahab's placement between them must have a purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p504/r2.anchor: After this, Im ām Far āhī has mentioned the wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r1.claim: The conquest sermon maps its three clauses to al-Kāfirūn, al-Naṣr, and al-Lahab: God's oneness, fulfilled promise, and defeat of enemies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r1.anchor: the subject matter of the three sūrahs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r2.claim: Most exegetes call al-Lahab Makkan because it answered Abū Lahab's insult at Ṣafā, but Islahi says this dating argument is unsound.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p505/r2.anchor: Most exegetes regard it to be a Makkan sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r1.speaker: Exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r1.claim: Exegetes report that at Ṣafā the Prophet warned his gathered Quraysh relatives of punishment and Abū Lahab retorted with a curse; they say this occasioned the sūrah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r1.anchor: Exegetes say that it is this incident

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r2.claim: Islahi accepts that the incident occurred but says it is improbable that the sūrah answered Abū Lahab and his wife's misconduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p506/r2.anchor: for various reasons it is improbable

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r1.claim: The revealed phrase is no tit-for-tat curse; Islahi says it carries no ring of condemnation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r1.anchor: These words in no way have a ring of condemnation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r2.claim: The opening predicts the end of Abū Lahab's political dominance, the defeat of his allies, and the loss of his pomp and wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r2.anchor: political dominance, a defeat of all his friends

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r3.claim: The opening is a prediction rather than a statement of a present fact.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r3.anchor: is not a statement of fact

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r4.claim: Because the truth had been conveyed conclusively, Islahi rejects an early Makkan date for the sūrah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r4.anchor: the truth had been communicated to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r5.claim: Since Abū Lahab died shortly after Badr, Islahi dates the prediction around that period and before his death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r5.anchor: He died a little after the battle of Badr

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r6.claim: The past tense expresses certainty about a future event.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p507/r6.anchor: The past tense adopted in the opening verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r1.claim: The Arabic root tabba means to perish or end in loss.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r1.anchor: to perish and end up in loss

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r2.claim: The idiom about both hands failing depicts complete helplessness and failure to attain an objective.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r2.anchor: both hands of such and such a person have failed to achieve an objective

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r3.claim: Fanad al-Zamānī's couplet uses breaking the hands of the arrogant to depict crushing their force.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r3.anchor: broke the hands of its ar rogant [people]

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r4.claim: The same arm-breaking idiom appears in Hebrew scripture, where Ezekiel describes Pharaoh's arms being broken.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p508/r4.anchor: In Hebrew, a sister language of Arabic, this idiom is used al so

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r1.claim: The verse predicts that Abū Lahab's political power will be crushed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r2.claim: His use of an honorific kunya is respectful, since Arabs generally use such a title out of respect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r2.anchor: when Arabs mention someone thus, it is generally out of respect for him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r3.claim: Abū Lahab alone among Quraysh opposed the Prophet to protect personal interests: as Baytullāh treasurer he diverted funds from the needy and pilgrims.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r3.anchor: He had taken such control of it that a greater part of the money received would go into his own pockets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r4.claim: Other Quraysh leaders objected to the attack on ancestral idols, respected the Prophet's moral teaching, and could have accepted a softer tone about idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p509/r4.anchor: They had great respect for the lofty morals

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r1.claim: Abū Lahab's self-interested enmity lacked the decency of principled disagreement; naming him exposes the character of truth's real enemies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r1.anchor:
interest s are
absolutely devoid of decency.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r2.claim: Religious allegiance, not bloodline, determines closeness to a prophet; Noah's son, Abraham's father, and Lot's wife illustrate this, making the mention a practical acquittal from unbelievers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r2.anchor: the religion of God. It is people who become the companions

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r3.claim: The first clause predicts Abū Lahab's political fall and the second his death; Badr and his humiliating smallpox death fulfilled both predictions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p510/r3.anchor: the second part is a predi ction of his own death.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r1.claim: Abū Lahab cowardly stayed home from Badr and sent a debtor in his place; the debtor likely died, but the scheme could not avert Abū Lahab's humiliating death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p511/r1.anchor: he forced a person from whom he had no hope of recovering a loan

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr leaves the hāʾ in أبي لهب unvocalized; the other readers vocalize it, and all use fatḥa in نارا ذات لهب.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: تبت يدا أبي لهب [المسد/ 1] ساكنة الهاء. وقرأ الباقون: أبي لهب محركة الهاء، ولم يختلفوا في فتح الهاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451#2/r2.claim: لهب and لهب can be dialect variants like سمع and سمع; shared fatḥa in the later occurrence makes fatḥa the stronger form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p451#2/r2.anchor: يشبه أن يكون: لهب ولهب، لغتين كالسمع والسمع، والنهر والنهر،

QIRAAT-ER:111:1:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:111:1:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:111:1:4#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on hāʾ changes lahab to lahb and may shift the sense from the act of flaming to flame as a concrete entity.
QIRAAT-ER:111:1:4#1/r1.anchor: This changes the vowel pattern from fa'al to fa'l

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406/r1.claim: Qatāda says Abū Lahab's hands were ruined and he himself was ruined.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p406/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ تبت يدا أبي لهب ﴾ قال خسرت يدا أبي لهب وخسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.claim: Following the prior sura's mass conversion, this one describes Abu Lahab as a loser who stayed outside the faith embraced by Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها دخول الناس في دين الله تعالى، أتبع بذكر من لم يدخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن جبير وعطاء ويمان بن رياب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r5.claim: They gloss tabbat as failed, lost, perished, strayed, or emptied of all good; the author says these meanings are close.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r5.anchor: وهنا قال ابن عباس: خابت، وقتادة: خسرت، وابن جبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r6.claim: Ruin is attributed to the hands because actions are mostly done with them, though the true object is the self, as in 22:10.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r6.anchor: وإسناد الهلاك إلى اليدين، لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r7.claim: Another view says Abu Lahab took a stone in his hands to throw at the Messenger, explaining the specific attribution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r7.anchor: وقيل: أخذ بيديه حجرا ليرمي به الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r8.claim: The apparent reading is an imprecation in tabbat followed by a report that it came to pass; Abd Allah's wa-qad tabb supports this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن التب دعاء، وتب: إخبار بحصول ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r9.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r9.claim: After 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet called relatives and Quraysh to warn them of punishment; Abu Lahab cursed the gathering, after which this sura was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p565/r9.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r1.claim: Abu Lahab's personal name was Abd al-Uzza; the author identifies his family relation to the Prophet.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن وابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r2.claim: They read Abu Lahab with a silent h; the other seven readers open it, while the fixed rhyme in dhata lahab keeps the opening vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وابن كثير: أبي لهب بسكون الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r3.claim: Zamakhshari calls the silent h a change in proper names, like the altered pronunciation of Shams Malik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهو من تغيير الأعلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r4.claim: The author says that explanation is not necessary: Abu Lahab is normally pronounced with an open h, and Shams Malik could simply have been named Shams from a plural form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r4.anchor: بل يمكن أن يكون مسمى بشمس المنقول من شمس الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r5.claim: Several explanations are offered for the kunya: his bright looks, its greater currency than his name, his destiny in fire, or its lower rank than a personal name; the last is linked to naming prophets rather than giving them kunyas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p566/r5.anchor: قيل: وكني بأبي لهب لحسنه وإشراق وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r1.claim: Surah al-Masad is Meccan and has five verses by unanimous agreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة المسد وهي مكية وآيها خمس بلا خلاف فى الامرين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r2.claim: One account links the surah to the previous one by following the mass conversion with the ruin of those who did not join Islam, bringing joy to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبل دخول الناس فى ملة الاسلام عقبه سبحانه بذكر هلاك بعض ممن لم يدخل فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r3.claim: Another account sees threat following promise and joy for the Prophet; the Imam connects the previous “your religion and mine” with promised victory for the Prophet and ruin for his uncle.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r3.anchor: وقيل هو من اتصال الوعيد بالوعد وفى كل مسرة له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال الامام في ذلك انه تعالى لما قال لكم دينكم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r4.speaker: الامام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r4.claim: The Imam says victory is the reward of the obedient while worldly loss and afterlife punishment answer the question about the disobedient; he calls the surah arrangement striking despite their distant revelation dates.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p259/r4.anchor: فكانه قيل الهى ما جزاء المطيع قال حصول النصر والفتح ثم قيل فما جزاء العاصى قال الخسار فى الدنيا والعقاب فى العقبى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r1.speaker: جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r1.claim: Jubayr and others explain “tabbat” as perished, comparable to the expression for an old woman ruined by age.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r1.anchor: أى هلكت كما قال جبير وغيره ومنه قولهم أشابة أم تابة يريدون أم هالكة من الهرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Qatada explain the word as loss; Ibn Abbas also glosses it as failure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r2.anchor: والتعجيز أى خسرت كما قال ابن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وعن الاول أيضا خابت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r3.speaker: يمان بن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r3.claim: Yaman ibn Waththab interprets the word as becoming empty of every good; the reported glosses are close in sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r3.anchor: وعن يمان بن وثاب صفرت من كل خير وهى على مافى فى البحر أقوال متقاربة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r4.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r4.claim: Al-Shihab traces the root to cutting, which leads to destruction; al-Raghib calls it continued loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r4.anchor: وقال الشهاب ان مادة التباب تدور على القطع وهو مؤد إلى الهلاك ولذا فسر به وقال الراغب هو الاستمرار فى الخسران

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r5.claim: Abu Lahab was Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet’s uncle and a fierce opponent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r5.anchor: هو عبد العزى عبد المطلب عم رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وكان شديد المعاداة والمناصبة له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r6.speaker: طارق المحاربى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r6.claim: A report from Tariq al-Muharibi recounts Abu Lahab following the young Prophet through Dhul-Majaz, throwing stones until his legs bled and calling him a liar.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r6.anchor: فى المجمع عن طارق المحاربى قال بينا أنا بسوق ذى المجاز اذا أنا برجل حديث السن يقول أيها الناس قولوا لااله الا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r7.claim: A report in the Two Sahihs and al-Tirmidhi says that when 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet called Quraysh from Safa, warned them of imminent punishment, and Abu Lahab cursed him, prompting this surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r7.anchor: وأخرج الامام أحمد والشيخان والترمذى عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت وأنذر عشيرتك الاقربين صعد النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على الصفا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r8.claim: Another version says Abu Lahab raised a stone to throw at the Prophet; the reports explain why the verse singles out his hands.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r8.anchor: ويروى أنه مع ذلك القول أخذ بيديه حجرا ليرمى بها رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عيه وسلم ومن هذا يعلم وجه ايثار التباب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r9.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits Ibn Abbas’s account that after leaving the ravine, Abu Lahab mocked the promised afterlife, inspected and blew on his hands, and cursed them; the surah was then revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r9.anchor: وكذا مما روى البيهقى فى الدلائل عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r10.claim: Tariq’s report particularly explains the reference to the two hands, which may be literal; the whole utterance curses both hands and the person.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r10.anchor: ومما روى عن طارق يعلم وجه الثانى فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r11.claim: The two clauses may instead state as fact that both his hands and he himself perished; the past tense marks certain fulfillment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r11.anchor: وجوز ان يكونا اخبارين بهلاك ذينك الامرين والتعبير بالماضى فى الموضعين لتحقق الوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r12.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r12.claim: Al-Farra says the first clause is a curse on the whole person, with “hands” as a metonym or part-for-whole figure; the author answers that whole-person usage is attested.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء الاول دعاء بهلاك جملته على ان اليدين اما كناية عن الذات والنفس لما بينهما من اللزوم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r1.claim: The reading transmitted from Ibn Abbas in the Two Sahihs, “and he has indeed perished,” makes the second clause factual, since “qad” does not precede supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r1.anchor: وفى الصحيحين وغيرهما من حديث ابن عباس فى سبب النزول فنزلت هذه السورة تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r2.claim: One explanation takes the first clause as the ruin of Abu Lahab’s work, which did not help him, and the second as the ruin of his person.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r2.anchor: وقيل الاول اخبار عن هلاك عمله حيث لم يفده ولم يمنعه لان الاعمال تزاول بالايدى غالبا والثانى اخبار عن هلاك نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r3.speaker: الماتريدى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r3.claim: Al-Maturidi reads “hands” as favors: Abu Lahab’s favors toward Muhammad and Quraysh were lost through enmity and Quraysh’s defeat, while the second clause predicts his death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r3.anchor: وفى التأويلات اليد بمعنى النعمة وكان يحسن إلى النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والى قريش

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r4.claim: Using Abu Lahab’s kunya publicizes the curse and fixes it as his lasting designation; other proposed motives include avoiding his ugly name, his flaming cheeks, wordplay, or a hell-bound allusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r4.anchor: وذكر بكنيته لاشتهاره بها وقد أريد تشهيره بدعوة السوء وان تبقى سمة له وذكره بأشهر علميه أوفق بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r5.claim: A rhetorical analysis treats Abu Lahab as an allusion to a person of Hell, since association with flame entails being hellish; scholars dispute whether the kunya’s literal sense is also intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r5.anchor: أو لجعله كناية عن الجهنمى فكأنه قيل تبت يدا جهنمى وذلك لان انتسابه إلى اللهب كانتساب الاب إلى الولد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r6.claim: Al-Sayyid’s claim that the kunya functions allusively only because Abu Lahab was famous by that name fails: such inference does not depend on a person’s fame.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p260#2/r6.anchor: وزعم السيد أيضا ان الكناية فدل أبى لهب لانه اشتهر بهذا الاسم وبكونه جهنميا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p261/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p261/r1.speaker: ابن محيص
ALUSI-FULL:v30p261/r1.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Kathir read Abu Lahab with a vowelless hāʾ; al-Zamakhshari calls it alteration of proper names, while Abu al-Baqaʾ regards it as a dialectal variant by the Kufan analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p261/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيص وابن كثير أبى لهب بسكون الهاء وهو من تغيير الاعلام على مافى الكشاف وقال أبو البقاء الفتح والسكون لغتان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r5.claim: Theological debate asks how Abu Lahab could be commanded to believe when the prediction that he will burn entails he will remain an unbeliever, seemingly requiring him to believe the contradictory claim that he will not believe.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r5.anchor: واستشكل أمر تكليف أبى لهب بالايمان مع قوله تعالى سيصلى الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r6.claim: One answer says he must believe the Prophet’s whole message in general, not every Quranic detail, so he need not believe the prediction about his own continued unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r6.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن ماكلفه هو الايمان بجميع ماجاء به النبى عليه الصلاة والسلام اجمالا لا الايمان بتفاصيل مانطق به القرآن الكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r7.claim: Another answer says the threat of Hell does not prove unbelief, since a sinner may enter for wrongdoing; this response does not work for the unbelievers addressed in al-Kafirun.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r7.anchor: بأن قوله تعالى سيصلى الخ ليس نصا فى أنه لايؤمن أصلا فان صلى النار غير مختص بالكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r8.speaker: الكعبى وأبو الحسين البصرى والقاضى عبد الجبار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r8.claim: Al-Kaʿbi, Abu al-Husayn al-Basri, and Qadi Abd al-Jabbar offer another answer, which the Imam rejects; the argument is deferred to longer theological works.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r8.anchor: وأجاب الكعبى وأبو الحسين البصرى وكذا القاضى عبد الجبار بغير ماذكر مما رده الامام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r9.claim: A further answer makes the threat conditional: he will burn if he dies without believing, so it does not explicitly say he will never believe.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p264#2/r9.anchor: وقيل فى خصوص هذه الآية أن المعنى سيصلى نارا ذات لهب ويخلد فيها ان مات ولم يؤمن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after the Prophet warned Quraysh of imminent punishment from Ṣafā, Abū Lahab cursed him for summoning them, and the surah was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم على الصفا فقال: يا صاحباه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r2.claim: Tabbat means Abū Lahab's hands failed and lost; hands stand for the whole person by the Arab practice of naming a part for the whole.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r2.anchor: قوله: {تبت} أي: خابت وخسرت يدا أبي لهب، [أي هو] (3) ، أخبر عن يديه، والمراد به نفسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r3.claim: Another explanation treats yad, hand, as an extra connective expression, like references to the hand of time or calamities.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: "اليد" صلة، كما يقال: يد الدهر ويد الرزايا والبلايا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r4.claim: A further explanation takes the hands as his wealth and possessions; the following wording signifies ruin and destruction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد بها ماله وملكه، يقال: فلان قليل ذات اليد، يعنون به المال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r5.claim: Abū Lahab was the Prophet's paternal uncle, named ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā; Muqātil says he was nicknamed Abū Lahab for his handsome, radiant face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r5.anchor: وأبو لهب: هو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 205/أواسمه عبد العزى. قال مقاتل: كني بأبي لهب لحسنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads Abī Lahab with a silent hāʾ, like nahr and nahr; the readers agree on fatḥa in dhāta lahab to match the verse endings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p578#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير "أبي لهب" ساكنة الهاء، وهي مثل: نهر ونهر. واتفقوا في "ذات لهب"

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r1.claim: Tabbat means perished or lost; tabab is loss leading to destruction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r1.anchor: هلكت أو خسرت والتباب خسران يؤدي إلى الهلاك

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r2.claim: The two hands mean Abu Lahab himself, as in 2:195; alternatively they refer to this world and the next.

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r3.claim: When 26:214 was revealed, Abu Lahab objected and picked up a stone to throw at Muhammad, and this surah then came down.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r3.anchor: جمع أقاربه فأنذرهم فقال أبو لهب: تبا لك ألهذا دعوتنا، وأخذ حجرا ليرميه به

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r4.claim: He is called Abu Lahab because the honorific was familiar, his personal name Abd al-Uzza was disliked, the epithet better suits a person of the Fire, or it echoes the phrase fire of flame.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r4.anchor: ولأن اسمه عبد العزى فاستكره ذكره، ولأنه لما كان من أصحاب النار كانت الكنية أوفق بحاله

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r5.claim: The reading Abu Lahab in the nominative is like saying Ali ibn Abu Talib.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r5.anchor: وقرىء «أبو لهب» كما قيل علي بن أبو طالب

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r6.claim: Wa tabb reports after the curse, using the past for a certain future as supported by a poetic line and a reading wa qad tabb; alternatively the first reports what his hands did and the second his own deeds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:1-3/r6.anchor: ويدل عليه أنه قرىء «وقد تب» أو الأول إخبار عما كسبت يداه والثاني عن عمل نفسه

BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.claim: The Prophet hoped that the reader of Tabbat would not be gathered with Abu Lahab in one abode.
BAYDAWI-FULL:111:5/r4.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة تبت رجوت أن لا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب في دار واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r1.claim: The surah decisively declares that even the closest unbeliever to a great victor will lose; this demonstrates the Lawgiver's unmatched sovereignty and urges all servants to affirm divine unity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r1.anchor: مقصودها البت والقطع الحتم بخسران الكافر ولو كان أقرب الخلق إلى أعظم الفائزين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r2.claim: Following al-Ikhlas, which is associated with promised victory and many helpers, the name Tabbat plainly signals this theme.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r3.claim: The basmala names God as the Compeller and Majestic, who misguides and guides; the Merciful gives communication to friend and foe, while the Compassionate singles out the beloved for guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567/r3.anchor: الذي عم الولي والعدو بنعمة البيان بعد الإكرام بالإيجاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r1.claim: The surah declares certain loss even for an unbeliever related to a victorious Prophet, showing God's unmatched sovereignty and calling all servants to monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r1.anchor: مقصودها البت والقطع الحتم بخسران الكافر ولو كان أقرب الخلق إلى أعظم الفائزين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r2.claim: Its placement after al-Ikhlas, associated with guaranteed victory and abundant supporters, and its name Tabbat signal its theme.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r3.claim: God's names in the basmala express majesty and guidance, universal communication to allies and enemies, and special guidance for those He favors.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#s111/r3.anchor: الذي عم الولي والعدو بنعمة البيان بعد الإكرام بالإيجاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r1.claim: After announcing victory and growing Muslim numbers, the preceding surah's closing name al-Tawwab prompts the question whether notorious Abu Lahab, Muhammad's close relative and fierce enemy, would change; this surah announces his ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r1.anchor: وكان أبو لهب - من ضدة العناد لهذا الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p567#2/r2.claim: Mentioning the nearest relative shows that neither kinship nor alliances saved the Quraysh; the claim fulfills al-Imran 12 and reminds Muhammad of the enemies' former power.
