IBNASHUR:111:1/r14.claim: Opening with destruction signals the sura's reproach and threat, a fitting opening for a satire, like a poem that begins by cursing its target.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r14.anchor: افتتاح السورة بالتبات مشعر بأنها نزلت لتوبيخ ووعيد

IBNASHUR:111:1/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r15.claim: The opening resembles the threat opening Surat al-Mutaffifin with the word woe.

IBNASHUR:111:1/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r16.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن الحكم
IBNASHUR:111:1/r16.claim: The opening line by ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam curses Qays for abandoning the Muslims' borders and turning away, illustrating a satiric opening of denunciation.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r16.anchor: قول عبد الرحمان بن الحكم من شعراء « الحماسة »

IBNASHUR:111:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r17.speaker: أبو تمام
IBNASHUR:111:1/r17.claim: Abu Tammam begins a satire with fire, disgrace, harm, and destruction, another opening that forecasts denunciation.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r17.anchor: قول أبي تمام في طالعة هجاء

IBNASHUR:111:1/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r18.speaker: أبو بكر بن الخازن
IBNASHUR:111:1/r18.claim: Abu Bakr ibn al-Khazin adapted that kind of forecast in the opening of a congratulatory poem on a birth.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r18.anchor: أخذ أبو بكر بن الخازن قوله في طالع قصيدة

IBNASHUR:111:1/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r19.claim: Tabb means loss and destruction; the wording is both a prayer and a rebuke, returning Abu Lahab's own insult against Muhammad as fitting recompense.

IBNASHUR:111:1/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r20.claim: An unassigned report says Abu Lahab took a stone to throw at the Prophet after insulting him; this explains why the curse names his hands.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r20.anchor: لما روي من أن أبا لهب لما قال للنبيء : « تباً لك سائر اليوم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r21.speaker: طارق المحاربي
IBNASHUR:111:1/r21.claim: Tariq al-Muharibi reports seeing Abu Lahab pursue Muhammad at Dhu al-Majaz, bloodying his legs while calling him a liar and warning people not to believe him.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r21.anchor: وروي عن طارق المحاربي قال : « بينا أنا بسوق ذي المجاز

IBNASHUR:111:1/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r22.claim: The hands are named because they caused the Prophet's harm; this resembles a curse wishing stones in the mouth of someone who says something offensive.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r22.anchor: فوقع الدعاء على يديه لأنهما سبب أذى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r23.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR:111:1/r23.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse invokes God's curse on the hands of people who withhold hospitality, illustrating a curse directed at hands as agents of action.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r23.anchor: قول النابغة : قعود الذي أبياتهم يثمدونهم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r24.speaker: أعرابي من بني أسد
IBNASHUR:111:1/r24.claim: An Asadi Bedouin's verse blesses Maswar's hands because they answered a call for aid, showing the opposite use of hands as instruments of help.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r24.anchor: وقال أعرابي من بني أسد : دعوت لما نابني

IBNASHUR:111:1/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r25.claim: Abu Lahab was ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle, and was also known as Abu ʿUtba after his son.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r25.anchor: وأبو لهب : هو عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب وهو عم النبي

IBNASHUR:111:1/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r26.claim: One reported explanation says he was called Abu Lahab in pre-Islamic times for his handsome, radiant face; Tariq's report and a similar report from Rabiʿa ibn ʿAbbad al-Dayli indicate the nickname was well known.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r26.anchor: فقيل :  كان يكنى بذلك في الجاهلية ( لحسنه وإشراق وجهه )

IBNASHUR:111:1/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r27.claim: The Qur'an may use his kunya instead of ʿAbd al-ʿUzza because that personal name invokes worship of al-ʿUzza, which the Qur'an does not endorse.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r27.anchor: فسماه القرآن بكنيته دون اسمه لأن في اسمه عبادة العزى

IBNASHUR:111:1/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r28.claim: Another explanation is that he was better known by his kunya than by his personal name.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r28.anchor: أو لأنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه العلم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r29.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r29.claim: The kunya also permits a pointed implication that he belongs to Hell, since lahab is the flame of a fire once its smoke has dissipated.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r29.anchor: أو لأن في كنيته ما يتأتى به التوجيه بكونه صائراً إلى النار

IBNASHUR:111:1/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r30.claim: Ab can denote someone devoted to or associated with what follows; the author uses familiar kunyas and Taftazani's account of names as omens to explain the suggestive Abu Lahab epithet.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r30.anchor: والأبُ :  يطلق على ملازم ما أضيف إليه

IBNASHUR:111:1/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r31.speaker: التفتزاني
IBNASHUR:111:1/r31.claim: Al-Taftazani's discussion of proper names and auspicious naming is cited to explain the kunya's implied association with Hell.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r31.anchor: كما أشار إليه التفتزاني في مبحث العَلَمِيَّة من « شرح المفتاح »

IBNASHUR:111:1/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r32.speaker: الشاعر
IBNASHUR:111:1/r32.claim: An anonymous poet jokes that Abu al-Mahasin has no son among his children, illustrating how a person's name can suggest an outcome that is not borne out literally.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r32.anchor:
وأنشد قول الشاعر :
قصدت أبا المحاسن كي أراه

IBNASHUR:111:1/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r33.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR:111:1/r33.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Lahab's daughter told the Prophet that people called her the daughter of the firewood of Hell, suggesting another possible sense of her father's kunya.

IBNASHUR:111:1/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r34.claim: Most readers pronounce lahab with a fatha; Ibn Kathir reads the h with sukun, a dialect form.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r34.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور لفظ { لهب } بفتح الهاء ، وقرأه ابن كثير بسكون الهاء

IBNASHUR:111:1/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r35.claim: The sukun may reflect the common Arabic tendency to suppress a vowel on a medial consonant after an initial consonant with a vowel.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r35.anchor: لأنهم كثيراً ما يسكنون عين الكلمة المتحركة مع الفاء

IBNASHUR:111:1/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r36.claim: Alternatively, the pronunciation may result from changing a vowel when a common noun becomes a proper name.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r36.anchor: وقد يكون ذلك لأن { لهب } صار جزءَ عَلَم والعرب قد يغيرون بعض حركات الاسم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r37.speaker: أبو الفتح بن جني
IBNASHUR:111:1/r37.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the altered vowel in Shums as a proper-name change, like Maʿdi Yakrib, Tahluk, and Mawhab.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r37.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جنيّ في كتاب « إعراب الحماسة »

IBNASHUR:111:1/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r38.claim: Abu Salma, Zuhayr's father's kunya, similarly has a changed vowel because Salma, originally a feminine name, was transferred to a man's name.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r38.anchor: وكما قالوا : أبو سلمى بضم السين كنية والد زهير

IBNASHUR:111:1/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r40.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r40.claim: The second clause may coordinate a curse on Abu Lahab himself with the prior curse on his hands, intensifying the rebuke; the whole and part meanings justify coordination.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r40.anchor: إما معطوفة على جملة :  { تبت يدا أبي لهب } عطف الدعاء على الدعاء

IBNASHUR:111:1/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r41.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r41.claim: Because the clauses differ as whole and part, their semantic difference licenses the conjunction; verbal emphasis would not be conjoined with waw, as discussed in Surat al-Kafirun.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r41.anchor: وتفيد بذلك تأكيداً لجملة :  { تبت يدا أبي لهب } لأنها بمعناها

IBNASHUR:111:1/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:111:1/r42.claim: Alternatively, the second clause is circumstantial with waw al-hal, not a prayer, but confirmation that the destruction invoked has occurred; the preceding line is then ridicule or a wish for more destruction.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r42.anchor: والواو واوَ الحال ولا تكون دعاءً إنما هي تحقيق لحصول ما دعي عليه به

IBNASHUR:111:1/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r43.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR:111:1/r43.claim: Al-Nabigha's line says that God did indeed repay ʿAdi with the stated punishment, illustrating a circumstantial clause that confirms a fulfilled outcome.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r43.anchor: كقول النابغة :  جزى ربه عني عدي بن حاتم

IBNASHUR:111:1/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r44.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR:111:1/r44.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading adds qad before tabb, supporting the circumstantial analysis and making the preceding words a taunt rather than a request for destruction.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r44.anchor: ويؤيد هذا الوجه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود « وقد تب »

IBNASHUR:111:1/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:111:1/r45.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
IBNASHUR:111:1/r45.claim: Ibn Rawaha's poem about his martyrdom at Mu'ta uses a prayer for guidance followed by confirmation that he was indeed guided, illustrating the circumstantial reading.
IBNASHUR:111:1/r45.anchor: كقول عبد الله بن رواحة حين خروجه إلى غزوة مؤتة

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan by consensus.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r1.anchor:
وهي مكية بإجماع .
روي في الحديث

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r2.claim: After 26:214, he told Safiyya and Fatima he could not avail them before God, summoned Quraysh at al-Ṣafā, asked if they would trust his warning of cavalry below, then warned of punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him, and the sūra followed.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r2.anchor: روي في الحديث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت عليه : { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين }

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r3.claim: Another report says that the Prophet loudly cried “O morning alarm!” as he summoned the people.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r3.anchor: وروي أنه صاح بأعلى صوته : «يا صباحاه »

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r4.claim: Tabbat means she was ruined or lost; tabāb means loss and destruction.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r4.anchor: و { تبت } معناه : خسرت ، والتباب : الخسار والدمار

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r5.claim: The loss is attributed to the hands because hands are where one earns and profits and gathers what one owns.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r5.anchor: وأسند ذلك إلى اليدين من حيث اليد موضع الكسب والربح ، وضم ما يملك

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r6.claim: The following declaration makes his ruin certain: it has been decreed for him that he has perished.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r6.anchor: ثم أوجب عليه أنه قد تب ، أي حتم ذلك عليه

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r7.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has “and he has surely perished” (وقد تب) instead of “and he perished” (وتب).
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r7.anchor: ففي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود :( تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب )

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r8.claim: Abu Lahab is Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal uncle.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r8.anchor: وأبو لهب : هو عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب ، وهو عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r9.claim: Despite being the Prophet's uncle, Abu Lahab had already been destined for wretchedness.

IBNATIYYA:111:1/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r10.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن والباقون
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin read the hāʾ of Abī Lahb without a vowel; the other readers vocalize it, and all use fatḥ in dhāti lahab.
IBNATIYYA:111:1/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن :( أبي لهْب ) بسكون الهاء ، وقرأ الباقون : بتحريك الهاء ، ولم يختلفوا في فتحها في { ذات لهب }

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Sūrat al-Masad as a Meccan sūra.

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r2.claim: In the Bukhari report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet calls Quraysh to gather at al-Batha, asks whether they would believe a warning of an imminent enemy, and warns of severe punishment; Abu Lahab objects that this was why they were gathered, curses the Prophet, and the sūra is revealed.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج إلى البطحاء

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r3.claim: An alternate wording has Abu Lahab shake dust from his hands and say, 'Perish you all day; was this why you gathered us?' before the revelation.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r3.anchor: وفي رواية : فقام ينفض يديه ،   وهو يقول : تبا لك سائر اليوم

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir distinguishes the first phrase as a prayer against Abu Lahab and the second as a statement that his ruin has occurred.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r4.anchor: الأول : دعاء عليه ،   والثاني : خبر عنه

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r5.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's paternal uncle, Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, also known by the kunya Abu Utba; he was nicknamed Abu Lahab for his shining face.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r5.anchor: واسمه : عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب ،   وكنيته أبو عتبة .   وإنما سمي " أبا لهب " لإشراق وجهه

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says Abu Lahab repeatedly harmed the Messenger, hated and scorned him, and belittled him and his religion.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r6.anchor: وكان كثير الأذية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والبغضة له

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r7.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r7.claim: Rabi'a ibn Abbad recalls seeing the Prophet preach that affirming God's oneness brings success in the market of Dhu al-Majaz, while Abu Lahab followed him calling him a lying Sabi. Abu Lahab was handsome, squint-eyed, and wore two braids; people identified him as the Prophet's uncle.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r7.anchor: ربيعة بن عباد ،   من بني الديل ،   وكان جاهليًا فأسلم - قال : رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الجاهلية في سوق ذي المجاز

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Ahmad alone transmits this account; Rabi'a says he was not a child then, since he could already carry a waterskin.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r8.anchor: قال أبو الزناد : قلت لربيعة : كنت يومئذ صغيرًا ؟ قال : لا والله

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r9.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r9.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's account reported by Rabi'a, the Prophet asks tribes to worship God alone, believe and protect him as he delivers God's message. Abu Lahab warns that the Prophet would make them abandon al-Lat, al-Uzza, and their allied jinn of Banu Malik ibn Uqays for innovation and misguidance, and urges them not to follow him. Ahmad and al-Tabarani also transmit this wording.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r9.anchor: سمعت ربيعة بن عباد الديلي يقول : إني لمع أبي رجل شاب

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir explains the first phrase as loss and failure, with Abu Lahab's deeds and efforts coming to nothing.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r10.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } أي : خسرت وخابت ،   وضل عمله وسعيه

IBNKATHIR:111:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r11.claim: The second phrase confirms that Abu Lahab's ruin and destruction have indeed occurred.
IBNKATHIR:111:1/r11.anchor: أي : وقد تب تحقق خسارته وهلاكه

KASHSHAF:111:1/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r1.claim: He identifies the sūra as Meccan and says it has five verses.

KASHSHAF:111:1/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r2.claim: Tabāb means destruction; the expression أشابة أم تابة describes someone ruined by old age and debility.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r2.anchor: التباب : الهلاك . ومنه قولهم : أشابة أم تابة ؟ أي : هالكة من الهرم والتعجيز .

KASHSHAF:111:1/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r3.claim: He initially interprets the phrase as a curse that Abu Lahab's hands perished.

KASHSHAF:111:1/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r4.claim: He takes wa-tabba as saying that Abu Lahab himself perished entirely.

KASHSHAF:111:1/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r5.claim: A report says Abu Lahab picked up a stone to throw at the Messenger, explaining the curse that his hands perish.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r5.anchor: لأنه فيما يروى : أخذ حجراً ليرمي به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:111:1/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r6.claim: Alternatively, his hands are made to perish, with the hands standing for his whole person; Zamakhsharī compares 22:10.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r6.anchor: أو جعلت يداه هالكتين . والمراد : هلاك جملته

KASHSHAF:111:1/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r7.claim: Alternatively, wa-tabba means that the matter happened and came to pass; he supports this completed-event sense with a poetic line ending وقد فعل.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r7.anchor: جَزَانِي جَزَاهُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ جَزَائِه *** جَزَاءَ الْكلاَبِ الْعَاوِيَاتِ وَقَدْ فَعَلْ

KASHSHAF:111:1/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:111:1/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads وقد تب, which Zamakhsharī cites to support the sense that the matter had indeed come to pass.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r8.anchor: ويدلّ عليه قراءة ابن مسعود : «وقد تب »

KASHSHAF:111:1/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r9.claim: A report says that after 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet called his clan at Ṣafā, tested whether they would believe a warning about cavalry at the mountain, then warned them of the Hour; Abu Lahab protested, and this sūra was revealed.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r9.anchor: وروي : أنه لما نزل { وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأقربين } [ الشعراء : 214 ]

KASHSHAF:111:1/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r10.claim: His first answer to why an ostensibly honorific kunya is used is that Abu Lahab was better known by it, making the hostile designation conspicuous and lasting.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r10.anchor: أن يكون مشتهراً بالكنية دون الاسم ، فقد يكون الرجل معروفاً بأحدهما

KASHSHAF:111:1/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r11.claim: A person may be known by either name or kunya, and the two can stand in apposition in either order.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r11.anchor: ولذلك تجري الكنية على الاسم ، أو الاسم على الكنية عطف بيان

KASHSHAF:111:1/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r12.speaker: غير مسمى
KASHSHAF:111:1/r12.claim: An unnamed reader has يدا أبو لهب, preserving the familiar form Abū Lahab and supporting the first explanation for using his kunya.

KASHSHAF:111:1/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r13.claim: He cites forms such as ʿAlī ibn Abū Ṭālib and Muʿāwiya ibn Abū Sufyān, where Abū is left unchanged so altering the familiar form will not confuse the hearer.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r13.anchor: كما قيل : علي بن أبو طالب . ومعاوية بن أبو سفيان ؛ لئلا يغير منه شيء فيشكل على السامع

KASHSHAF:111:1/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r14.claim: He illustrates the importance of familiar name forms with Meccan governor Fulayta ibn Qasim's two sons, both called ʿAbd Allāh, one marked genitive and the other accusative; a Meccan man was known only by the genitive form.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r14.anchor: ولفليتة بن قاسم أمير مكة ابنان ، أحدهما : عبد الله ، بالجرّ ، والآخر عبد الله ، بالنصب .

KASHSHAF:111:1/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r15.claim: A second explanation is that Abu Lahab's personal name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, so the kunya was used in its place.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r15.anchor: والثاني : أنه كان اسمه عبد العزّى ، فعدل عنه إلى كنيته .

KASHSHAF:111:1/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r16.claim: A third explanation is that his fate in a fire with flames matches his kunya, making it fitting to name him by it.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r16.anchor: والثالث : أنه لما كان من أهل النار ، ومآله إلى نار ذات لهب ، وافقت حاله كنيته

KASHSHAF:111:1/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r17.claim: Abū Lahab can function as a trait-based label, like Abū al-Sharr for an evil person and Abū al-Khayr for a good one.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r17.anchor: ويقال : أبو لهب ، كما يقال : أبو الشر ، للشرير . وأبو الخير ، للخير

KASHSHAF:111:1/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r18.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:111:1/r18.claim: As an example of a trait-based kunya, the Messenger called Abū al-Muhallab Abū Ṣafra because of the yellow color in his face.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r18.anchor: كما كنى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا المهلب : أبا صفرة ، بصفرة في وجهه .

KASHSHAF:111:1/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r19.speaker: غير مسمى
KASHSHAF:111:1/r19.claim: An alternative account says he was called Abū Lahab for his flushed, radiant cheeks.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r19.anchor: وقيل : كنى بذلك لتهلب وجنتيه وإشراقهما

KASHSHAF:111:1/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:111:1/r20.claim: Zamakhsharī suggests that using the kunya this way could mock Abu Lahab and his pride in his bright cheeks.
KASHSHAF:111:1/r20.anchor: فيجوز أن يذكر بذلك تهكماً به ، وبافتخاره بذلك .

KASHSHAF:111:1/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:111:1/r21.speaker: غير مسمى
KASHSHAF:111:1/r21.claim: A reading gives أبي لهب with sukūn; Zamakhsharī treats it as an alteration of proper names, like saying Shams ibn Mālik with ḍamma.

MAWARDI:111:1/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r1.claim: Al-Māwardī identifies Sūrat al-Masad as Meccan.
MAWARDI:111:1/r1.anchor: سورة المسد مكية بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم

MAWARDI:111:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI:111:1/r2.claim: Abū Lahab asked what he would receive for believing; when told he would receive what Muslims receive, he rejected a religion that made him their equal, and the verse was revealed.
MAWARDI:111:1/r2.anchor: حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن أبا لهب أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

MAWARDI:111:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:111:1/r3.claim: After the warning to his near relatives, the Prophet called people to al-Ṣafā and warned of imminent punishment; Abū Lahab cursed him, and the sūra was revealed.
MAWARDI:111:1/r3.anchor: ما رواه ابن عباس أنه لما نزل { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفا

MAWARDI:111:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
MAWARDI:111:1/r4.claim: Abū Lahab turned visiting delegations away by calling the Prophet a lying sorcerer or mad; after one delegation persisted, he again maligned the Prophet, who grieved and received this sūra.
MAWARDI:111:1/r4.anchor: ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان أنه كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفد انطلق إليهم أبو لهب

MAWARDI:111:1/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:111:1/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses تَبَّتْ as having failed or come to naught.

MAWARDI:111:1/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r6.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI:111:1/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains تَبَّتْ as having gone astray.

MAWARDI:111:1/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI:111:1/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr explains تَبَّتْ as having perished.

MAWARDI:111:1/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r8.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
MAWARDI:111:1/r8.claim: Yamān ibn Riʾāb says تَبَّتْ means becoming empty of every good thing.
MAWARDI:111:1/r8.anchor: الرابع : صفِرت من كل خير ،   قاله يمان بن رئاب .

MAWARDI:111:1/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r9.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
MAWARDI:111:1/r9.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits from Abū ʿAmr a chant reportedly heard after ʿUthmān’s killing, ending with an imprecation using تَبًّا.
MAWARDI:111:1/r9.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان بن عفان سمع الناس هاتفاً يقول :

MAWARDI:111:1/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:111:1/r10.claim: Qatāda glosses تَبَّتْ as having lost; the cited anonymous verse uses تَبًّا in a curse.
MAWARDI:111:1/r10.anchor: الخامس : خسرت ،   قاله قتادة ،   ومنه قول الشاعر : تواعَدَني قوْمي ليَسْعوْا

MAWARDI:111:1/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r11.claim: One reading takes Abū Lahab’s two hands to mean Abū Lahab himself, since a person may be expressed by the hand; the cited phrase in 22:10 likewise means the person.
MAWARDI:111:1/r11.anchor: يعني نفس أبي لهب ،   وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد ،   كما قال تعالى { ذلك بما قدمت يداك }

MAWARDI:111:1/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r12.claim: An alternative takes the hands as Abū Lahab’s deeds, which are attributed to the hands because actions are usually performed with them.
MAWARDI:111:1/r12.anchor: أي عمل أبي لهب ،   وإنما نسب العمل إلى اليد ؛ لأنه في الأكثر يكون بها .

MAWARDI:111:1/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r13.claim: It is said that Abū Lahab was given this kunya for his beauty and his glowing, flame-like cheeks.
MAWARDI:111:1/r13.anchor: وقيل : إنه كني أبا لهب لحسنه وتلهب وجنته ،

MAWARDI:111:1/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r14.claim: One explanation for using Abū Lahab’s kunya is that he was better known by it than by his personal name.
MAWARDI:111:1/r14.anchor: أنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه

MAWARDI:111:1/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r15.claim: Another explanation is that his given name identified him as a servant of an idol, reportedly ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, so the sūra avoids it.
MAWARDI:111:1/r15.anchor: لأنه كان مسمى بعبد صنم ،   وقيل : إنه عبد العزى ،   فلذلك عدل عنه .

MAWARDI:111:1/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r16.claim: A third explanation says a personal name is nobler than a kunya, which refers to someone through another person; God therefore names His prophets by their names.
MAWARDI:111:1/r16.anchor: لأن الاسم أشرف من الكنية ؛ لأن الكنية إشارة إليه باسم غيره ،   ولذلك دعا الله أنبياءه بأسمائهم .

MAWARDI:111:1/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r17.claim: One view takes وَتَبَّ as emphasis repeating the preceding curse on Abū Lahab’s hands.
MAWARDI:111:1/r17.anchor: أنه تأكيد للأول من قوله :{ تبت يدا أبي لهب } ، فقال بعده :

MAWARDI:111:1/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI:111:1/r18.claim: Another view says his hands were ruined when God prevented him from harming the Messenger, while he himself perished through the painful punishment awaiting him with God.
MAWARDI:111:1/r18.anchor: يعني تبت يدا أبي لهب بما منعه الله تعالى من أذى لرسوله ،   وتب بما له عند الله من أليم عقابه .

MAWARDI:111:1/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:111:1/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes وَتَبَّ to mean that Abū Lahab had already perished.
MAWARDI:111:1/r19.anchor: يعني قد تبّ ،   قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI:111:1/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r20.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:111:1/r20.claim: Mujāhid interprets وَتَبَّ to mean that Abū Lahab’s offspring also perished.
MAWARDI:111:1/r20.anchor: يعني وتبّ ولد أبي لهب ،   قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI:111:1/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r21.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:111:1/r21.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads وقد تب instead of وَتَبَّ, making the ending a statement; the other reading is a curse like the opening.
MAWARDI:111:1/r21.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( تبت يدا أبي لهبٍ وقد تب ) ، جعله خبراً ،

MAWARDI:111:1/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:111:1/r22.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abū Lahab’s hands perished away from monotheism.
MAWARDI:111:1/r22.anchor: أحدهما : عن التوحيد ،   قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI:111:1/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:111:1/r23.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:111:1/r23.claim: Mujāhid says Abū Lahab’s hands perished away from good deeds.

NASAFI:111:1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r1.claim: Nasafi identifies Sūrat Abī Lahab as Meccan and says it has five verses.
NASAFI:111:1/r1.anchor: سورة أبي لهب مكية ، وهي خمس آيات

NASAFI:111:1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r2.claim: Tabba means ruin; an Arabic expression he cites describes someone ruined by old age, and he glosses the hands as perished.
NASAFI:111:1/r2.anchor: التباب : الهلاك ، ومنه قولهم : أشابّة أم تابّة ، أي هالكة من الهرم

NASAFI:111:1/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r3.claim: An unattributed report says Abu Lahab picked up a stone to throw at the Prophet, explaining the ruin of his hands.
NASAFI:111:1/r3.anchor: لأنه فيما يروى أخذ حجراً ليرمي به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI:111:1/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r4.claim: Nasafi also glosses وَتَبَّ as meaning that Abu Lahab himself perished completely.

NASAFI:111:1/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r5.claim: Alternatively, the hands are made ruined while the intended meaning is the ruin of his whole person, as in the expression cited from 22:10.
NASAFI:111:1/r5.anchor: أو جعلت يداه هالكتين ، والمراد هلاك جملته ، كقوله { بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ }

NASAFI:111:1/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r6.claim: Nasafi glosses وَتَبَّ as “that happened and came to pass”; the quoted poetic line uses وقد فعل to illustrate this sense.

NASAFI:111:1/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI:111:1/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading وَقَد تَبَّ supports the sense that the ruin had indeed come to pass.
NASAFI:111:1/r7.anchor: وقد دلت عليه قراءة ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : { وَقَد تَبَّ }

NASAFI:111:1/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r8.claim: After 26:214 was revealed, Muhammad summoned Quraysh at Ṣafā, elicited their trust in his warning, warned them of the Hour, and Abu Lahab rebuked him; this sūra was then revealed.
NASAFI:111:1/r8.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل :{ وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } رقى الصفا

NASAFI:111:1/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r9.claim: The kunya is an honorific, used because Abu Lahab was better known by it than by his personal name.
NASAFI:111:1/r9.anchor: وإنما كناه والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بها دون الاسم

NASAFI:111:1/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r10.claim: Another explanation is that he was given a kunya to avoid his disliked personal name, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.
NASAFI:111:1/r10.anchor: أو لكراهة اسمه ، فاسمه عبد العزى

NASAFI:111:1/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI:111:1/r11.claim: A further explanation is that his fate in a fire of flames made the kunya fit his condition.
NASAFI:111:1/r11.anchor: أو لأن مآله إلى نار ذات لهب فوافقت حاله كنيته

NASAFI:111:1/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:111:1/r12.speaker: مكي
NASAFI:111:1/r12.claim: Nasafi attributes the form أبي لهب to the Meccan reader (Makkī).
NASAFI:111:1/r12.anchor: فوافقت حاله كنيته . { أَبِي لَهَبٍ } مكي

QURTUBI:111:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r1.claim: Qurtubi says the sura is Meccan by consensus and has five verses.
QURTUBI:111:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية بإجماع ، وهي خمس آيات .

QURTUBI:111:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:111:1/r2.claim: In the report of Ibn Abbas found in the two Sahih collections, Muhammad gathers his clans at al-Safa after the command to warn his closest kin, asks whether they would believe a warning of approaching cavalry, and warns of severe punishment; Abu Lahab curses him for summoning them, and the sura is revealed.
QURTUBI:111:1/r2.anchor: في الصحيحين وغيرهما -واللفظ لمسلم- عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت ( " وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين "

QURTUBI:111:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r3.speaker: الحميدي وغيره
QURTUBI:111:1/r3.claim: The added account says Abu Lahab's wife comes with a hand-sized stone, but God veils Muhammad from her sight so she sees only Abu Bakr; she threatens to strike Muhammad and recites a rhyme denouncing him.
QURTUBI:111:1/r3.anchor: زاد الحميدي وغيره : فلما سمعت امرأته ما نزل في زوجها وفيها من القرآن

QURTUBI:111:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:111:1/r4.claim: The Prophet says Quraysh abuse and satirize ‘Mudhammam’ while he is Muhammad, and marvels that God has diverted their harm from him.
QURTUBI:111:1/r4.anchor: وكانت قريش إنما تسمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مذمما ، يسبونه ، وكان يقول :

QURTUBI:111:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI:111:1/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd reports that Abu Lahab asked what he would receive if he believed; when told he would receive what other Muslims receive, he rejected a religion that made him their equal, and the sura was revealed.
QURTUBI:111:1/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن سبب نزولها ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن أبا لهب أتى النبي

QURTUBI:111:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
QURTUBI:111:1/r6.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan says Abu Lahab repeatedly turned visiting delegations away by calling Muhammad a lying magician; when one group insisted on meeting him, Abu Lahab cursed him, Muhammad was saddened, and the sura was revealed.
QURTUBI:111:1/r6.anchor: وقول ثالث حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان قال : كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:111:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:111:1/r7.claim: Another account says Abu Lahab tried to throw a stone at the Prophet, God prevented him, and this sura was revealed because of that prevention.
QURTUBI:111:1/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا لهب أراد أن يرمي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر ، فمنعه الله من ذلك

QURTUBI:111:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:111:1/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tabbat as ‘failed’ or ‘disappointed.’

QURTUBI:111:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r12.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
QURTUBI:111:1/r12.claim: Yaman ibn Riʾab says tabbat means she was left empty of every good thing.
QURTUBI:111:1/r12.anchor: وقال يمان بن رئاب : صفرت من كل خير .

QURTUBI:111:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r13.speaker: الأصمعي، أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI:111:1/r13.claim: Al-Asmaʿi reports that after Uthman was killed, a voice recited a poem lamenting how people deserted him and saying ‘tabban’ of what they did; the verse illustrates the word's use.
QURTUBI:111:1/r13.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان رحمه الله سمع الناس هاتفا يقول :

QURTUBI:111:1/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r14.claim: The hands are specified because people do most work with them: his hands were ruined, and he himself was ruined.
QURTUBI:111:1/r14.anchor: وخص اليدين بالتباب ؛ لأن العمل أكثر ما يكون بهما ، أي خسرتا وخسر هو .

QURTUBI:111:1/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r15.claim: An alternative takes ‘hands’ to mean Abu Lahab himself, since Arabic can use a part for the whole; Qurtubi links this to 22:10.
QURTUBI:111:1/r15.anchor: وقيل : المراد باليدين نفسه . وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد ، كما قال الله تعالى : { بما قدمت يداك }

QURTUBI:111:1/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r16.claim: Qurtubi calls part-for-whole expression common Arabic usage, as in saying time's hand or calamities' hands struck someone, and cites a poet's ‘hand of disasters.’
QURTUBI:111:1/r16.anchor: تقول : أصابته يد الدهر ، ويد الرزايا والمنايا

QURTUBI:111:1/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r17.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:111:1/r17.claim: Al-Farra says the first tabban is a curse or prayer for destruction and the second is a factual report, like ‘May God destroy him; he has perished.’
QURTUBI:111:1/r17.anchor: قال الفراء : التب الأول دعاء ، والثاني خبر ، كما يقال : أهلكه الله وقد هلك .

QURTUBI:111:1/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r18.speaker: عبد الله، أُبي
QURTUBI:111:1/r18.claim: Abdullah and Ubayy read the second clause as ‘and he has indeed perished.’
QURTUBI:111:1/r18.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله وأبي " وقد تب "

QURTUBI:111:1/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r19.claim: Abu Lahab's given name was Abd al-Uzza; he was the Prophet's paternal uncle. His wife, al-Awraʾ Umm Jamil, was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb's sister, and both were fiercely hostile to Muhammad.
QURTUBI:111:1/r19.anchor: وأبو لهب اسمه عبد العزى ، وهو ابن عبد المطلب عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . وامرأته العوراء أم جميل

QURTUBI:111:1/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r20.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
QURTUBI:111:1/r20.claim: Tariq ibn Abd Allah al-Muharibi recalls hearing Muhammad preach at the market of Dhu al-Majaz while a man behind him bloodied his legs and called him a liar; bystanders identified that man as Abu Lahab.
QURTUBI:111:1/r20.anchor: قال طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي : إني بسوق ذي المجاز ، إذ أنا بإنسان يقول : " يا أيها الناس ، قولوا لا إله إلا الله

QURTUBI:111:1/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:111:1/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Lahab claimed Muhammad had bewitched people, contrasting their ordinary hunger with Muhammad's having fed them a sheep's thigh and quenched them with a large jug of milk.
QURTUBI:111:1/r21.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو لهب : سحركم محمد ، إن أحدنا ليأكل الجذعة

QURTUBI:111:1/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r22.claim: Qurtubi rejects the claim that Allah's calling this pagan by a kunya proves that it is generally acceptable to give unbelievers kunyahs.
QURTUBI:111:1/r22.anchor: وقد ظن قوم أن في هذا دليلا على تكنية المشرك ، وهو باطل

QURTUBI:111:1/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r23.claim: One reason Allah used Abu Lahab's kunya rather than his given name is that the latter was Abd al-Uzza, and Allah does not ascribe servanthood in Scripture to an idol.
QURTUBI:111:1/r23.anchor: الأول : أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى ، والعزى : صنم ، ولم يضف الله في كتابه العبودية إلى صنم

QURTUBI:111:1/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r24.claim: A second reason is that Abu Lahab was more widely known by his kunya than by his given name.
QURTUBI:111:1/r24.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه ، فصرح بها .

QURTUBI:111:1/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r25.claim: A third reason is that a given name is nobler than a kunya, so Allah lowered him to the lesser form; prophets are addressed by their names.
QURTUBI:111:1/r25.anchor: الثالث : أن الاسم أشرف من الكنية ، فحطه الله عز وجل عن الأشرف إلى الأنقص

QURTUBI:111:1/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r26.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r26.claim: The fourth reason is that Allah makes him literally the father of the Flame by consigning him to it, fulfilling the ominous name and portent he chose for himself.
QURTUBI:111:1/r26.anchor: الرابع : أن الله تعالى أراد أن يحقق نسبته ، بأن يدخله النار ، فيكون أبا لها

QURTUBI:111:1/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r27.speaker: author
QURTUBI:111:1/r27.claim: Another explanation says his family called him Abu Lahab because his face glowed with beauty; God redirected them from flattering names such as Abu al-Nur and Abu al-Diya to the blameworthy ‘flame,’ then made the Fire his abode.
QURTUBI:111:1/r27.anchor: وقد قيل : اسمه كنيته . فكان أهله يسمونه أبا لهب ، لتلهب وجهه وحسنه

QURTUBI:111:1/r28.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r28.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، ابن كثير، ابن محيصن
QURTUBI:111:1/r28.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Muhaysin read Abī Lahab with a still hāʾ; they all keep the hāʾ in dhāt lahab open to preserve the verse endings.
QURTUBI:111:1/r28.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وابن كثير وابن محيصن :{ أبي لهب } بإسكان الهاء

QURTUBI:111:1/r29.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r29.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:111:1/r29.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when God created the Pen and commanded it to record what would exist, the decree ‘Perished the hands of Abu Lahab’ was among what it wrote.
QURTUBI:111:1/r29.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما خلق الله عز وجل القلم قال له : اكتب ما هو كائن

QURTUBI:111:1/r30.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r30.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:111:1/r30.claim: Asked by Mansur whether Abu Lahab could have escaped the Fire if his fate was in the Preserved Record, Hasan says he could not; it was written before Abu Lahab and his parents were created.
QURTUBI:111:1/r30.anchor: وقال منصور : سئل الحسن عن قوله تعالى : { تبت يدا أبي لهب } ، هل كان في أم الكتاب ؟

QURTUBI:111:1/r31.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r31.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:111:1/r31.claim: In the Adam-and-Moses report, Moses reproaches Adam for leading people from Paradise; Adam replies that God had written the matter before creating the heavens and earth, and the Prophet says Adam prevailed over Moses.
QURTUBI:111:1/r31.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " فحج آدم

QURTUBI:111:1/r32.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r32.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:111:1/r32.claim: In Hammam's report from Abu Hurayra, Adam says Moses found in the Torah that it was written two thousand years before Adam's creation that Adam would disobey his Lord and go astray; Adam asks why Moses blames him for a prewritten act.
QURTUBI:111:1/r32.anchor: وفي حديث همام عن أبي هريرة أن آدم قال لموسى : " بكم وجدت الله كتب التوراة قبل أن يخلقني ؟

QURTUBI:111:1/r33.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:111:1/r33.speaker: طاووس، ابن هرمز، الأعرج، أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:111:1/r33.claim: A report through Tawus, Ibn Hurmuz, and al-Aʿraj from Abu Hurayra gives a different interval: the Torah's writing preceded creation by forty years.
QURTUBI:111:1/r33.anchor: وفي حديث طاووس وابن هرمز والأعرج عن أبي هريرة : ( بأربعين عاما )

RAZI:111:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r1.claim: After creation for worship and Sūrat al-Kāfirūn’s contrast between Muḥammad’s obedience and the unbelievers’ idolatry, al-Naṣr promises the obedient victory and reward, while al-Masad depicts the disobedient’s worldly loss and punishment hereafter.
RAZI:111:1/r1.anchor: ثم بين في سورة : { قل يا أيها الكافرون }

RAZI:111:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r2.claim: The disparity between people’s worldly fortunes is a test of what God gives; the sinner faces swift punishment, while the obedient receives forgiveness and mercy.

RAZI:111:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:111:1/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after three hidden years, Muḥammad summoned his nearest kin from al-Ṣafā per 26:214, said he could not aid them without monotheism, and Abū Lahab’s curse occasioned the sūrah.
RAZI:111:1/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان رسول الله يكتم أمره في أول المبعث ويصلي في شعاب مكة ثلاث سنين

RAZI:111:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r4.claim: A second occasion report says Muḥammad called the Quraysh to al-Ṣafā with “O morning alarm”; after they affirmed they would believe his warning of an approaching enemy, Abū Lahab cursed him and the sūrah was revealed.
RAZI:111:1/r4.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صعد الصفا ذات يوم

RAZI:111:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r5.claim: A third report says Muḥammad gathered his uncles for a meal; they scorned its small appearance, ate their fill while little food vanished, and Abū Lahab rejected the invitation to Islam.
RAZI:111:1/r5.anchor: أنه جمع أعمامه وقدم إليهم طعاما في صحفة

RAZI:111:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r6.claim: In a related version Abū Lahab asked what he would gain by becoming Muslim; Muḥammad said what Muslims receive, and Abū Lahab rejected a religion that made him equal to others.
RAZI:111:1/r6.anchor: وروي أنه قال أبو لهب : فمالي إن أسلمت

RAZI:111:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r7.claim: A fourth report says Abū Lahab dissuaded visiting delegations by calling Muḥammad a sorcerer or mad; one delegation insisted on meeting him, and Muḥammad was saddened by the insult before the sūrah descended.
RAZI:111:1/r7.anchor: كان إذا وفد على النبي وفد سألوا عمه عنه

RAZI:111:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r8.claim: One explanation is destruction: Arabic usage calls an aged, ruined woman “shāba tība,” and the verse about Pharaoh’s plot says it ended in ruin.

RAZI:111:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r9.speaker: الأعرابي
RAZI:111:1/r9.claim: A Bedouin who had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan said, “I am ruined and have ruined her”; the Prophet did not object, supporting the sense of destruction.
RAZI:111:1/r9.anchor: أن الأعرابي لما واقع أهله في نهار رمضان

RAZI:111:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r10.claim: If an act belongs to faith or is its weakest part, abandoning it brings ruin; Abū Lahab’s abandonment of belief, speech, and action, together with false belief, speech, and action, certainly merits that meaning.
RAZI:111:1/r10.anchor: ففي حق أبي لهب حصل ترك الاعتقاد والقول والعمل

RAZI:111:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r11.claim: A second explanation is “she lost”: tabāb is loss that ends in destruction, as in the verse saying they increased people only in loss.
RAZI:111:1/r11.anchor: التباب هو الخسران المفضي إلى الهلاك

RAZI:111:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:111:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains tabbat as frustration: Abū Lahab’s trusted status once let him turn visitors away from Muḥammad, but his later hostility made his accusations suspect and defeated his aim.
RAZI:111:1/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لأنه كان يدفع القوم عنه

RAZI:111:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r13.claim: The mention of the hand may reflect Abū Lahab’s habit of putting a hand on visitors’ shoulders and pushing them away while calling Muḥammad mad.
RAZI:111:1/r13.anchor: ولعله إنما ذكر اليد لأنه كان يضرب بيده على كتف الوافد عليه

RAZI:111:1/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r14.speaker: عطاء
RAZI:111:1/r14.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains tabbat as “was defeated”: Abū Lahab thought his hand was uppermost and expected to expel, humiliate, and overpower Muḥammad.
RAZI:111:1/r14.anchor: عن عطاء تبت أي غلبت لأنه كان يعتقد أن يده هي العليا

RAZI:111:1/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r15.speaker: ابن وثاب
RAZI:111:1/r15.claim: Ibn Waththāb explains the hands as left empty of every good.
RAZI:111:1/r15.anchor: عن ابن وثاب ؛ صفرت يداه على كل خير

RAZI:111:1/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r16.speaker: طارق المحاربي
RAZI:111:1/r16.claim: Ṭāriq al-Muḥāribī reports seeing Muḥammad preach in the market while a man behind him stoned him until his heels bled and called him a liar; people identified the man as Abū Lahab.
RAZI:111:1/r16.anchor: روي عن طارق المحاربي أنه قال : رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI:111:1/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r17.claim: “Hands” can mean the whole person, as in Qurʾānic expressions about what one’s hands have sent ahead or what God’s hands made, and in the proverb “your hands tied it.”
RAZI:111:1/r17.anchor: المراد من اليدين الجملة كقوله تعالى : { ذلك بما قدمت يداك }

RAZI:111:1/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r18.claim: Other explanations take “his hands” as his religion and worldly and future fortunes, or as the means of bringing benefit and warding off harm.
RAZI:111:1/r18.anchor: تبت يداه أي دينه ودنياه أولاه وعقباه

RAZI:111:1/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r19.claim: Another explanation is that one hand is a weapon and the other a shield.
RAZI:111:1/r19.anchor: أو لأن اليمنى سلاح والأخرى جنة

RAZI:111:1/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r20.claim: A report says Muḥammad visited Abū Lahab at night to invite him again; after a kid goat miraculously praised the Prophet, Abū Lahab tore its hands and cursed it, which occasioned the verse.
RAZI:111:1/r20.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام لما دعاه نهارا فأبى

RAZI:111:1/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r21.speaker: محمد بن إسحق
RAZI:111:1/r21.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that Abū Lahab mocked Muḥammad’s promises about the afterlife, blew on his empty hands, and said he saw nothing in them.
RAZI:111:1/r21.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحق : يروى أن أبا لهب كان يقول

RAZI:111:1/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r22.claim: One analysis makes the first clause an imprecation and the second a factual report that it came true, supported by Ibn Masʿūd’s reading “and he was indeed ruined.”
RAZI:111:1/r22.anchor: أنه أخرج الأول مخرج الدعاء عليه

RAZI:111:1/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r23.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI:111:1/r23.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the second clause as “wa-qad tabb,” “and he was indeed ruined,” supporting the factual reading.
RAZI:111:1/r23.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن مسعود وقد تب

RAZI:111:1/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r24.claim: A second analysis takes both clauses as reports: the first says Abū Lahab’s deeds perished, the second that he himself perished.
RAZI:111:1/r24.anchor: كل واحد منهما إخبار ولكن أراد بالأول هلاك عمله

RAZI:111:1/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r25.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:111:1/r25.claim: Abū Muslim reads the first clause as his wealth and the second as Abū Lahab himself, comparing it with people who lose themselves and their families.

RAZI:111:1/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r26.claim: A fourth reading makes the first clause Abū Lahab himself and the second his son ʿUtba.
RAZI:111:1/r26.anchor: { تبت يدا أبى لهب } يعني نفسه

RAZI:111:1/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r27.claim: A report says ʿUtba blasphemed to Muḥammad and spat at him; after the Prophet prayed for a beast to attack him, a lion killed him on a journey to Syria.
RAZI:111:1/r27.anchor: اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك

RAZI:111:1/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r28.claim: Although the sūrah preceded ʿUtba’s death and uses past tense, Rāzī says it reports what God already knew would happen.
RAZI:111:1/r28.anchor: لأنه كان في معلومه تعالى أنه يحصل ذلك

RAZI:111:1/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r29.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r29.claim: A fifth analysis says Abū Lahab’s hands perished because he failed to recognize his Lord’s right, and he himself perished because he failed to recognize the Messenger’s right.

RAZI:111:1/r30.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r30.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r30.claim: A reading with nominative “Abū Lahab” supports treating the kunya as a proper name, answering why he is called Lahab despite having no son by that name.

RAZI:111:1/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r31.claim: Because Abū Lahab functions as his name, the kunya need not carry its usual connotation of honor.
RAZI:111:1/r31.anchor: أنه لما كان اسما خرج عن إفادة التعظيم

RAZI:111:1/r32.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r32.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r32.claim: Another answer is that the kunya replaced his birth name, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.
RAZI:111:1/r32.anchor: أنه كان اسمه عبد العزى فعدل عنه إلى كنيته

RAZI:111:1/r33.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r33.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r33.claim: The kunya may suit his fate in a flaming fire, like calling a wicked person “father of evil.”
RAZI:111:1/r33.anchor: أنه لما كان من أهل النار ومآله إلى نار ذات لهب وافقت حاله كنيته

RAZI:111:1/r34.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r34.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r34.claim: Alternatively, “Abū Lahab” may mockingly describe his glowing, flame-colored cheeks and belittle him.

RAZI:111:1/r35.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r35.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r35.claim: Though Muḥammad was merciful, Abū Lahab obstructed his message by calling him mad; confronting the trusted uncle made his hostility discredit his accusations.
RAZI:111:1/r35.anchor: كان يصرف الناس عن محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI:111:1/r36.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r36.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r36.claim: Muḥammad’s bluntness showed that he would make no religious concession even for an uncle who stood in place of his father.
RAZI:111:1/r36.anchor: أن محمدا لو كان يداهن أحدا في الدين ويسامحه فيه

RAZI:111:1/r37.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r37.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r37.claim: Kinship would normally demand compassion, but Abū Lahab’s extreme hostility merited an equally severe rebuke.
RAZI:111:1/r37.anchor: فلما انقلب الأمر وحصلت العداوة العظيمة

RAZI:111:1/r38.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r38.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r38.claim: The Prophet is not told “say” this because his uncle’s kinship warrants deference; the unbelievers in al-Kāfirūn were not his uncles.
RAZI:111:1/r38.anchor: لأن قرابة العمومة تقتضي رعاية الحرمة

RAZI:111:1/r39.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r39.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r39.claim: In al-Kāfirūn the unbelievers attacked God, so God told Muḥammad to answer; here they attacked Muḥammad, so God answers Abū Lahab directly.
RAZI:111:1/r39.anchor: أن الكفار في تلك السورة طعنوا في الله

RAZI:111:1/r40.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r40.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r40.claim: A third answer is that Muḥammad’s silence lets God defend him, consistent with the instruction that the servants of the Merciful answer ignorant people peacefully.
RAZI:111:1/r40.anchor: لما شتموك ، فاسكت حتى تندرج تحت هذه الآية

RAZI:111:1/r41.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r41.speaker: أبو بكر
RAZI:111:1/r41.claim: A report about Abū Bakr says the Prophet explained that while Abū Bakr stayed silent, an angel answered his insulter; when he replied, the angel left and Satan came.
RAZI:111:1/r41.anchor: يروى أن أبا بكر كان يؤذيه واحد فبقي ساكتا

RAZI:111:1/r42.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r42.speaker: author
RAZI:111:1/r42.claim: Rāzī takes the report as a lesson: God defends and aids whoever does not answer a fool directly.
RAZI:111:1/r42.anchor: أن من لا يشافه السفيه كان الله ذابا عنه

RAZI:111:1/r43.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r43.speaker: ابن كثير المكي
RAZI:111:1/r43.claim: Ibn Kathīr of Mecca reads the hāʾ of “Lahab” without a vowel; Abū ʿAlī says Lahab/Lahab are dialectal variants, like ash-shamʿ and an-nahr.
RAZI:111:1/r43.anchor: قراءة عبد الله بن كثير المكي حيث كان يقرأ : { أبي لهب } ساكنة الهاء

RAZI:111:1/r44.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r44.speaker: أبو علي
RAZI:111:1/r44.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the two forms are dialect variants, but the open hāʾ is preferable because other occurrences have it open.
RAZI:111:1/r44.anchor: يشبه أن يكون لهب ولهب لغتين كالشمع والشمع والنهر والنهر ، وأجمعوا في قوله : { سيصلى نارا ذات لهب } على فتح الهاء

RAZI:111:1/r45.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:111:1/r45.speaker: غيره
RAZI:111:1/r45.claim: Another scholar says the hāʾ is open in the later occurrence to match the sūrah’s rhyme.
RAZI:111:1/r45.anchor: وقال غيره : إنما اتفقوا على الفتح في الثانية مراعاة لوفاق الفواصل
